translations.literal: Zhu Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu.

sentences.zh: 王遜，字邵伯，魏興人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xun, courtesy name Shaobo, was a native of Weixing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun of Weixing bore the courtesy name Shaobo.

sentences.zh: 仕郡察孝廉，為吏部令史，轉殿中將軍。

translations.literal: Recommended filial and incorrupt at his commandery, he served as clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and was promoted palace army commander.
translations.idiomatic: County nomination raised him to ministry clerk, then imperial guards captain.

sentences.zh: 累遷上洛太守。

translations.literal: Promoted repeatedly to administrator of Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to governor Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 私牛馬在郡生駒犢者，秩滿悉以付官，雲是郡中所產也。

translations.literal: Private cattle and horses that foaled or calved in the commandery—when his term ended he delivered them all to the treasury, saying they were produced within the jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Any beasts bred under his rule he surrendered at term’s end as county-born stock.

sentences.zh: 轉魏興太守。

translations.literal: Transferred to administrator of Weixing.
translations.idiomatic: Next he governed Weixing.

sentences.zh: 惠帝末，西南夷叛，甯州刺史李毅卒，城中百餘人奉毅女固守經年。

translations.literal: Near Emperor Hui’s end southwestern barbarians rebelled; Inspector of Ningzhou Li Yi died, and little over a hundred people in the city upheld Yi’s daughter in defense for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Southwestern tribes rose as Hui tottered; Li Yi fell at Ningzhou, leaving a hundred defenders rallying around his daughter for a year.

sentences.zh: 永嘉四年，治中毛孟詣京師求刺史，不見省。

translations.literal: In Yongjia’s fourth year Administrator Mao Meng traveled to the capital seeking an inspector but received no audience.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia 4 sent Mao Meng pleading at Luoyang—court ignored him.

sentences.zh: 孟固陳曰：「君亡親喪，幽閉窮城，萬里訴哀，不垂湣救。

translations.literal: Meng firmly argued: “Your lordship lost kin and lies trapped in a beleaguered city; though we wail across myriad leagues you grant no compassionate rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Meng protested: “Rulers perish while cities choke—we shout leagues away yet mercy never stirs.

sentences.zh: 既慚包胥無哭秦之感，又愧梁妻無崩城之驗，存不若亡，乞賜臣死。

translations.literal: We shame Shen Baoxu who lacked tears enough for Qin and blush before Liang Qi lacking proof she collapsed walls—to survive brings less honor than death; grant me execution.
translations.idiomatic: We lack Shen Baoxu’s tears before Qin or widow Liang’s collapsing grief—living now dishonors dying—strike me dead.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷憐之，乃以遜為南夷校尉、甯州刺史，使于郡便之鎮。

translations.literal: ” The court pitied him and appointed Xun colonel of southern barbarians and inspector of Ningzhou, letting him proceed straight from the commandery to his post.
translations.idiomatic: ” Moved, court named Xun southern colonel and Ningzhou inspector with mandate from county seat onward.

sentences.zh: 與孟俱行，道遇寇賊，逾年乃至。

translations.literal: Together with Meng they went; robbers waylaid them along the road—more than a year passed before arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits harried their march beyond a year.

sentences.zh: 外逼李雄，內有夷寇，吏士散沒，城邑丘墟。

translations.literal: Pressed by Li Xiong without and tribal raiders within, clerks and troops scattered; towns lay ruined heaps.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong strangled supply lines while tribes ravaged within until garrisons vanished into ash heaps.

sentences.zh: 遜披荒糾厲，收聚離散，專杖威刑，鞭撻殊俗。

translations.literal: Xun cleared wasteland, tightened discipline, gathered refugees, relying solely on fearful punishments and flogging alien customs.
translations.idiomatic: He hacked roads from ruin, welded law through terror, herded exiles with scourges tuned to frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 遜未到州，遙舉董聯為秀才，建甯功曹周悅謂聯非才，不下版檄。

translations.literal: Before reaching the province he remotely nominated Dong Lian as cultivated talent; Jianning aide Zhou Yue judged Lian unworthy and refused to issue summons.
translations.idiomatic: Still en route he tapped Dong Lian as xiucai; Zhou Yue withheld commission.

sentences.zh: 遜既到，收悅殺之。

translations.literal: Once arrived Xun seized Yue and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Arrival meant Yue’s arrest and blade.

sentences.zh: 悅弟潛謀殺遜，以前建甯太守趙混子濤代為刺史。

translations.literal: Yue’s brother Qian plotted to murder Xun and install Zhao Tao—son of former Jianning Administrator Zhao Hun—as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Qian schemed assassination and Zhao Tao’s coup.

sentences.zh: 事覺，並誅之。

translations.literal: The plot surfaced; all were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Exposure doomed every conspirator.

sentences.zh: 又誅豪右不奉法度者數十家。

translations.literal: He further executed dozens of powerful houses that flouted statute.
translations.idiomatic: Magnates mocking law numbered dozens beheaded.

sentences.zh: 征伐諸夷，俘馘千計，獲馬及牛羊數萬餘，於是莫不振服，威行寧土。

translations.literal: Campaigning against tribal bands he took heads by the thousand and horses, cattle, and sheep beyond tens of thousands—thereafter none dared resist; awe blanketed Ning lands.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier strikes piled trophies—thousands of skulls, myriad herds—until submission rippled province-wide.

sentences.zh: 又遣子澄奉表勸進於元帝，帝嘉之，累加散騎常侍、安南將軍、假節，校尉、刺史如故，賜爵褒中縣公。

translations.literal: He sent son Cheng with memorial urging Yuan Di’s accession; the emperor praised him, promoting him repeatedly to palace attendant regular, general who pacifies the south, holding credential staff—colonel and inspector unchanged—with noble rank Duke of Baozhong county.
translations.idiomatic: Son Cheng’s accession memorial won stacks of titles—palace rider, southern pacifier, credential bearer—plus Baozhong duke.

sentences.zh: 遜以地勢形便，上分牂柯為平夷郡，分硃提為南廣郡，分建甯為夜郎郡，分永昌為梁水郡，又改益州郡為晉寧郡，事皆施行。

translations.literal: Judging terrain advantageous he memorialized to split Zangke into Pingyi commandery, Zhuti into Nanguang, Jianning into Yelang, Yongchang into Liangshui, and rename Yizhou commandery Jining—all approved.
translations.idiomatic: He carved new commands—Pingyi, Nanguang, Yelang, Liangshui—and rechristened Yizhou as Jining—throne stamped each map.

sentences.zh: 先是，越巂太守李釗為李雄所執，自蜀逃歸，遜復以釗為越巂太守。

translations.literal: Earlier Administrator of Yuegui Li Zhao had been captured by Li Xiong but fled Shu back south; Xun reappointed Zhao Yuegui governor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhao escaped Xiong’s cage to Shu margins; Xun restored his Yuegui seal.

sentences.zh: 李雄遣李驤、任回攻釗，釗自南秦與漢嘉太守王載共距之，戰於溫水，釗敗績，載遂以二郡附雄。

translations.literal: Li Xiong dispatched Li Xiang and Ren Hui against Zhao; Zhao joined Administrator of Hanjia Wang Zai from southern Qin to resist, fought at Warm Water, suffered rout, and Zai surrendered both commands to Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong’s generals shattered Zhao at Warm Water; Wang Zai handed twin prefectures to Cheng.

sentences.zh: 後驤等又渡瀘水寇寧州，遜使將軍姚崇、爨琛距之，戰於堂狼，大破驤等，崇追至瀘水，透水死者千餘人。

translations.literal: Later Xiang crossed the Lu River raiding Ningzhou; Xun sent Generals Yao Chong and Cuan Chen to resist at Tanglang, crushing Xiang; Chong pursued to the Lu—over a thousand drowned crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang forded Lu and fell to Yao Chong’s Tanglang trap—corpses jammed the ford.

sentences.zh: 崇以道遠不敢渡水，遜以崇不窮追也，怒囚群帥，執崇，鞭之，怒甚，發上沖冠，冠為之裂，夜中卒。

translations.literal: Chong feared distance and dared not ford; Xun, furious he failed to pursue, imprisoned commanders, seized Chong, and flogged him—rage lifted his cap pins until the cap tore—he died that night.
translations.idiomatic: Chong halted at Lu banks; Xun flogged him until hairpins snapped—apoplexy killed him overnight.

sentences.zh: 遜在州十四年，州人復立遜中子堅行州府事。

translations.literal: Xun spent fourteen years in the province; locals enthroned his middle son Jian to manage prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen years later provincials raised middle heir Jian as steward.

sentences.zh: 詔除堅為南夷校尉、甯州刺史、假節，諡遜曰壯。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Jian southern colonel and Ningzhou inspector with credential staff; Xun received posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The court confirmed Jian's seal and gave Wang Xun the posthumous title Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 陶侃懼堅不能抗對蜀人，太寧末，表以零陵太守尹奉為寧州，征堅還京，病卒。

translations.literal: Tao Kan feared Jian could not withstand Shu; late Taining he memorialized Lingling Administrator Yin Feng for Ningzhou and summoned Jian to the capital—Jian died en route.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan doubted Jian’s spine—late Taining swapped in Yin Feng; Jian perished traveling east.

sentences.zh: 兄澄襲爵，曆魏興太守、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Elder brother Cheng inherited the title, serving as Weixing governor and palace attendant regular.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Cheng took the dukedom through Weixing and palace posts.

sentences.zh: 蔡豹，字士宣，陳留圉城人。

translations.literal: Cai Bao, courtesy name Shixuan, was from Yucheng in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Bao styled Shixuan hailed from Chenliu’s Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖質，漢衛尉，左中郎將邕之叔父也。

translations.literal: His ninth-generation ancestor Zhi had been Han superintendent of the guards—uncle of Palace Gentleman Cai Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestor Zhi commanded Han guards—kin to Cai Yong.

sentences.zh: 祖睦，魏尚書。

translations.literal: Grandfather Mu was Wei minister of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Mu ran Wei’s secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父宏，陰平太守。

translations.literal: Father Hong governed Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: Father Hong held Yinping.

sentences.zh: 豹有氣幹，曆河南丞，長樂、清河太守。

translations.literal: Bao possessed energy and capacity; he served as aide of Henan, then administrators of Changle and Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Capable and bold, he filled Henan aide and twin governorships.

sentences.zh: 避亂南渡，元帝以為振武將軍、臨淮太守，遷建威將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Fleeing turmoil southward, Yuan Di named him general who rouses might and administrator of Linhuai, later general who builds might and inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Flight south won him rousing-might general, Linhuai governor, then building-might general atop Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，祖逖為徐州，豹為司馬，素易豹。

translations.literal: Earlier Zu Ti led Xuzhou while Bao was his adjutant—Ti had always slighted Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti once commanded Xuzhou with Bao as major—Ti sneered.

sentences.zh: 至是，逖為豫州，而豹為徐州，俱受征討之寄，逖甚愧之。

translations.literal: Now Ti held Yuzhou while Bao held Xuzhou; both bore expedition mandates—Ti felt mortified.
translations.idiomatic: Now equals in border commands, Ti smarted.

sentences.zh: 是時太山太守徐龕與彭城內史劉遐同討反賊周撫於寒山，龕將於藥斬撫。

translations.literal: Then Taishan Administrator Xu Kan with Pengcheng interior secretary Liu Xia jointly campaigned against rebel Zhou Fu at Hanshan; Kan’s officer Yu Yao beheaded Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Taishan’s Xu Kan and Pengcheng’s Liu Xia attacked Zhou Fu at Hanshan; Yu Yao took Fu’s head.

sentences.zh: 及論功，而遐先之。

translations.literal: When merit was tallied Xia ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Credit lists placed Xia ahead.

sentences.zh: 龕怒，乙太山叛，自號安北將軍、兗州刺史，攻破東莞太守侯史旄而據其塢。

translations.literal: Kan in fury seized Taishan, rebelled, styled himself general who pacifies the north and inspector of Yanzhou, stormed Dongguan Administrator Hou Shi Mao’s fort, and seized the redoubt.
translations.idiomatic: Kan rebelled as northern pacifier, cracked Dongguan’s Hou Shi Mao, and squatted his bastion.

sentences.zh: 石季龍伐之，龕懼，求降，元帝許焉。

translations.literal: Shi Hu attacked him; Kan feared and sued for surrender—Yuan Di accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu’s pressure broke Kan into submission—court OK’d.

sentences.zh: 既而復叛歸石勒，勒遣其將王伏都、張景等數百騎助龕。

translations.literal: Soon he rebelled again to Shi Le; Le sent generals Wang Fudu and Zhang Jing with several hundred riders to aid Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Kan flipped back to Shi Le; Le lent cavalry captains.

sentences.zh: 詔征虜將軍羊鑒、武威將軍侯禮、臨淮太守劉遐、鮮卑段文鴦等與豹共討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered General Who Conquers Barbarians Yang Jian, General Who Displays Might Hou Li, Linhuai Administrator Liu Xia, Xianbei Duan Wenying and others to join Bao in punishing him.
translations.idiomatic: Court tasked Yang Jian, Hou Li, Liu Xia, Duan Wenying, and Bao with Kan’s ruin.

sentences.zh: 諸將畏懦，頓兵下邳，不敢前。

translations.literal: Generals cowered, halting troops at Xiapi, daring not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Coalition froze at Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 豹欲進軍，鑒固不許。

translations.literal: Bao wished to march; Jian stubbornly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Bao pressed attack; Jian vetoed.

sentences.zh: 龕遣使請救於勒，勒辭以外難，而多求於龕。

translations.literal: Kan sent envoys begging rescue from Le; Le pleaded outer crises yet demanded endless gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Kan begged Le; Le invented excuses while squeezing tribute.

sentences.zh: 又王伏都等淫其室。

translations.literal: Moreover Wang Fudu and cohort ravished Kan’s household.
translations.idiomatic: Le’s riders raped Kan’s women.

sentences.zh: 龕知勒不救，且患伏都等縱暴，乃殺之，復求降。

translations.literal: Kan knew Le would not save him and could not endure Fudu’s excess—he slew them and sued again to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Kan slaughtered Le’s captains and renewed capitulation.

sentences.zh: 元帝惡其反覆不納，敕豹、鑒以時進討。

translations.literal: Yuan Di despised the flip-flopping and refused; he ordered Bao and Jian to advance on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Throne spurned another fake surrender—ordered attack.

sentences.zh: 鑒及劉遐等並疑憚不相聽從，互有表聞，故豹久不得進。

translations.literal: Jian and Liu Xia hesitated, ignoring orders, each memorializing separately—Bao could not move for months.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual suspicion clogged paperwork—Bao stalled.

sentences.zh: 尚書令刁協奏曰：「臣等伏思淮北征軍已失不速，今方盛暑，冒涉山險，山人便弓弩，習土俗，一人守厄，百夫不當。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Diao Xie memorialized: “We reflect that the Huai-north expedition already missed speed; now midsummer forces march mountain defiles where locals wield crossbows—one man guarding a pass stops a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie warned: “Summer columns crossing tribal ridges face ambush archers—single chokepoints swallow armies.

sentences.zh: 且運漕至難，一朝糧乏，非復智力所能防禦也。

translations.literal: Moreover river supply is desperately hard—should grain fail overnight no wit can defend.
translations.idiomatic: River logistics snap easily—starvation erases strategy.

sentences.zh: 《書》云寧致人，不致於人。

translations.literal: The 《Documents》 says it is better to draw the enemy here than to be drawn there.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Documents》 counsels making the foe come to you rather than rushing into his trap.

sentences.zh: 宜頓兵所在，深壁固壘，至秋不了，乃進大軍。

translations.literal: We should halt where we stand, deepen walls and strengthen ramparts; if autumn ends without decision then commit the main host.
translations.idiomatic: Park troops, thicken walls, strike after harvest if needed.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「知難而退，誠合兵家之言。

translations.literal: ” An edict replied: “Retreating when difficulty appears fits military doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: ” Edict answered: “Withdrawal on hardship matches canon.

sentences.zh: 然小賊雖狡猾，故成擒耳。

translations.literal: Yet petty bandits, however cunning, remain catchable.
translations.idiomatic: Small prey still snares.

sentences.zh: 未戰而退，先自摧衄，亦古之所忌。

translations.literal: To quit without battle first breaks our own spine—also taboo in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Unbloodied retreat shames ancient wisdom.

sentences.zh: 且邵存已據賊壘，威勢既振，不可退一步也。

translations.literal: Moreover Shao Cun already holds the rebel fort—momentum surges; not one step backward.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Cun grips Kan’s nest—advance only.

sentences.zh: 」於是遣治書御史郝嘏為行台，催攝令進討。

translations.literal: ” Therefore they dispatched supervising secretary Hao Jia as mobile headquarters to spur the offensive.
translations.idiomatic: ” Court fired Hao Jia east to whip generals.

sentences.zh: 豹欲徑進，鑒執不聽。

translations.literal: Bao wanted a direct thrust; Jian still refused.
translations.idiomatic: Bao demanded frontal strike—Jian blocked.

sentences.zh: 協又奏免鑒官，委豹為前鋒，以鑒兵配之，降號折沖將軍，以責後效。

translations.literal: Xie again memorialized to strip Jian’s office, appoint Bao vanguard, attach Jian’s troops to him, and demote Bao’s rank to general who smashes charge to redeem merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xie cashiered Jian, handed his men to Bao as crack general—demotion pending victory.

sentences.zh: 豹進據卞城，欲以逼龕。

translations.literal: Bao advanced to occupy Biancheng to press Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao seized Biancheng to pinch Kan.

sentences.zh: 時石季龍屯钜平，將攻豹，豹夜遁。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Shi Hu camped at Juping preparing against Bao—Bao fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu loomed at Juping—Bao bolted.

sentences.zh: 退守下邳。

translations.literal: He fell back to defend Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: He hugged Xiapi walls.

sentences.zh: 徐龕襲取豹輜重于檀丘，將軍留寵、陸黨力戰，死之。

translations.literal: Kan raided Bao’s baggage train at Tanqiu; generals Liu Chong and Lu Dang fought to death.
translations.idiomatic: Kan looted Tanqiu trains—Liu Chong and Lu Dang died holding line.

sentences.zh: 豹既敗，將歸謝罪，北中郎王舒止之，曰：「胡寇方至，使君且當攝職，為百姓障捍。

translations.literal: Defeated, Bao meant to return and confess; northern commander Wang Shu stopped him: “Barbarians approach—hold office awhile and shield the people.
translations.idiomatic: Shu counseled: “Nomads loom—cling to command, shield folk.

sentences.zh: 賊退謝罪，不晚也。

translations.literal: After bandits withdraw confession will not be late.
translations.idiomatic: Resign after crisis ebbs.

sentences.zh: 」豹從之。

translations.literal: ” Bao obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Bao stayed.

sentences.zh: 元帝聞豹退，使收之。

translations.literal: Yuan Di hearing of Bao’s retreat ordered his arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Throne ordered Bao seized.

sentences.zh: 使者至，王舒夜以兵圍豹，豹以為他難，率麾下擊之，聞有詔乃止。

translations.literal: Envoys arrived; Shu surrounded Bao by night—Bao mistook another crisis and struck until edict clarified.
translations.idiomatic: Shu’s midnight cordon looked like mutiny until imperial voice clarified.

sentences.zh: 舒執豹，送至建康，斬之，屍於市三日，時年五十二。

translations.literal: Shu seized Bao, escorted him to Jiankang, executed him, exposed corpse three days—age fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang execution followed—corpse hung market three days at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 豹在徐土，內撫將士，外懷諸眾，甚得遠近情，聞其死，多悼惜之。

translations.literal: In Xu lands Bao soothed troops within and tribes without—north and south cherished him; mourning spread at news of death.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and settlers mourned his fairness.

sentences.zh: 無子，兄子裔字元子，散騎常侍、兗州刺史、高陽鄉侯。

translations.literal: Childless, nephew Yi styled Yuanzi became palace attendant regular, inspector of Yanzhou, Marquis of Gaoyang township.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Yi inherited fame—palace rider, Yanzhou inspector, Gaoyang marquis.

sentences.zh: 殷浩北伐，使裔率眾出彭城，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Yin Hao’s northern expedition sent Yi leading troops from Pengcheng—he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao’s war consumed Yi at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 劉胤，字承胤，東萊掖人，漢齊悼惠王肥之後也，美姿容，善自任遇，交結時豪，名著海岱間，士咸慕之。

translations.literal: Liu Yin, courtesy name Chengyin, was from Ye in Donglai—descended from Han Prince Dao-Hui of Qi—handsome, confident, befriended magnates, famed between sea and Tai heights—scholars idolized him.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome Liu Yin of Donglai, Qi royal blood, dazzled coastal elites.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良，辟司空掾，並不就。

translations.literal: Recommended worthy and incorrupt, summoned aide to the minister of works—he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: Court nominations went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 且天下大亂，攜母欲避地遼東，路經幽州，刺史王浚留胤，表為渤海太守。

translations.literal: As chaos engulfed the realm he escorted mother toward Liaodong; passing Youzhou Inspector Wang Jun detained Yin, memorializing him administrator of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Flight toward Liaodong trapped him under Wang Jun’s Bohai appointment.

sentences.zh: 浚敗，轉依冀州刺史邵續。

translations.literal: After Jun fell he attached to Ji Inspector Shao Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Jun’s collapse drove him to Shao Xu.

sentences.zh: 續徒眾寡弱，謀降于石勒，胤言于續曰：「夫田單、包胥，齊楚之小吏耳，猶能存已滅之邦，全喪敗之國。

translations.literal: Xu’s host was weak and plotted surrender to Shi Le; Yin told Xu: “Tian Dan and Shen Baoxu were petty clerks of Qi and Chu yet restored extinguished states and rescued ruined realms.
translations.idiomatic: Yin pleaded: “Tian Dan and Shen Baoxu were clerks yet rebuilt kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 今將軍杖精銳之眾，居全勝之城，如何墜將登之功於一蕢，委忠信之人於豺狼乎！

translations.literal: Now you wield crack troops inside an undefeated city—how cast aside merit nearing crown for one basketful or abandon loyal hearts to jackals!
translations.idiomatic: Why junk victory-in-hand to jackals?

sentences.zh: 且項羽、袁紹非不強也，高祖縞冠，人應如響；

translations.literal: Moreover Xiang Yu and Yuan Shao were hardly weak—yet Gaozu in hemp cap drew responses like echoes;
translations.idiomatic: Tyrants fell before Liu Bang’s plain cap;

sentences.zh: 曹公奉帝，而諸侯綏穆。

translations.literal: Cao Cao upheld the emperor and lords grew calm.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao’s imperial puppet soothed lords.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 蓋逆順之理殊，自然之數定也。

translations.literal: Because principle of rebellion versus loyalty differs—Heaven’s arithmetic fixes outcome.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous mandate decides fate.

sentences.zh: 況夷戎丑類，屯結無賴，雖有犬羊之盛，終有庖宰之患，而欲托根結援，無乃殆哉！

translations.literal: How much more barbarian scum huddling without honor—though numerous as dogs and sheep they face butcher’s block—yet you would root with them—perilous indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Alien packs swarm yet await slaughter—allying courts doom.

sentences.zh: 」續曰：「若如君言，計將安出？

translations.literal: ” Xu asked, “If so, what plan?
translations.idiomatic: ” Xu pressed strategy.

sentences.zh: 」胤曰：「琅邪王以聖德欽明，創基江左，中興之隆可企踵而待。

translations.literal: ” Yin answered: “Prince Langya shines with sagely virtue, founding east of the Yangzi—restoration stands within sight.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yin urged Langya prince’s rising mandate eastward.

sentences.zh: 今為將軍計者，莫若抗大順以激義士之心，奉忠正以厲軍人之志。

translations.literal: For the general now nothing surpasses upholding grand legitimacy to stir gentlemen’s hearts and displaying loyalty to steel soldiers’ resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Wave righteous banner—steel men’s spines.

sentences.zh: 夫機事在密，時至難違，存亡廢興，在此舉矣。

translations.literal: Opportunity lies in secrecy; moments flee—survival or ruin hangs on this act.
translations.idiomatic: Secret timing seals destiny.

sentences.zh: 」續從之，乃殺異議者數人，遣使江南，朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: ” Xu followed—executed dissenters, sent envoys south—the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xu slew doubters, hailed Jin court—praise followed.

sentences.zh: 胤仍求自行，續厚遣之。

translations.literal: Yin still asked to go in person, and Xu generously sent him forth.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin again asked to travel on his own behalf, and Shao Xu sent him off with generous support.

sentences.zh: 既至，元帝命為丞相參軍，累遷尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: When he had arrived, Emperor Yuan ordered him to be an aide to the Chancellor of State; he was repeatedly promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the court, Emperor Yuan appointed him aide to the Chancellor of State and later promoted him repeatedly to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 胤聞石季龍攻厭次，言於元帝曰：「北方鎮皆沒，惟余邵續而已。

translations.literal: Yin heard that Shi Jilong was attacking Yanqi and said to Emperor Yuan: "The northern garrison towns have all fallen; only Shao Xu remains.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yin learned that Shi Jilong was assaulting Yanqi, he told Emperor Yuan: "Every northern bastion is gone except Shao Xu.

sentences.zh: 如使君為季龍所制，孤義士之心，阻歸本之路。

translations.literal: If you, sir, were restrained by Jilong, you would isolate the hearts of righteous men and block the roads by which they return to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: If you fall under Jilong's thumb, you will strand loyal hearts and cut off the routes home for those who would serve the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜存救援。

translations.literal: In my foolish opinion it is fitting to preserve him with rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view we should send relief and keep him alive.

sentences.zh: 」元帝將遣救之，會續已沒而止。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yuan was about to dispatch rescue when it happened that Xu had already perished, so he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Yuan was ready to send aid, but Shao Xu had already fallen, so the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 王敦素與胤交，甚欽貴之，請為右司馬。

translations.literal: Wang Dun had long been on friendly terms with Yin and greatly esteemed him; he requested Yin as Right Major Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun had always been close to Liu Yin and held him in high regard; he asked to have Yin serve as Right Major Clerk.

sentences.zh: 胤知敦有不臣心，枕疾不視事，以是忤敦意，出為豫章太守，辭以腳疾，詔就家授印綬。

translations.literal: Yin knew Dun harbored a heart not loyal to the throne, so he feigned illness on his pillow and avoided duty; thereby offending Dun's wishes, he was sent out as Administrator of Yuzhang; pleading foot ailment, he declined, but an edict ordered the seal cord conferred at his home.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin saw that Wang Dun nursed treasonous ambitions, so he stayed bedridden and refused to handle affairs; Wang Dun took offense, transferred him to Yuzhang as administrator, and when Yin cited bad feet the throne ordered the seals delivered to his house regardless.

sentences.zh: 郡人莫鴻，南土豪族，因亂，殺本縣令，橫恣無道，百姓患之。

translations.literal: A man of the commandery named Mo Hong, a powerful southern clan, exploited the turmoil to kill the county magistrate; he behaved lawlessly and the common people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Hong of the commandery, a wealthy southern magnate, used the chaos to murder the sitting magistrate and terrorized the district until the people groaned under him.

sentences.zh: 胤至，誅鴻及諸豪右，界內肅然。

translations.literal: When Yin arrived, he executed Hong and the leading magnates, and within his borders all was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin executed Mo Hong and the rest of the local strongmen, and the jurisdiction fell quiet.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，為平南軍司，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianhe era he became Army Supervisor of the South Pacifying Army with additional appointment as Palace Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianhe reign he was named army supervisor under the general Who Pacifies the South and was also given the title of ordinary attendant cavalier at court.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻作亂，溫嶠率眾而下，留胤等守溢口。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, Wen Qiao led the host downstream and left Yin and others to guard Yikou.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Jun's revolt, Wen Qiao marched downstream while Liu Yin and others were left to hold Yikou.

sentences.zh: 事平，以勳賜爵豐城子。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was granted the noble rank Viscount of Fengcheng for merit.
translations.idiomatic: After peace returned he received the merit title of Viscount of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 俄而代嶠為平南將軍、都督江州諸軍事、領江州刺史、假節。

translations.literal: Soon he succeeded Qiao as general Who Pacifies the South, commander of all military affairs of Jiangzhou, concurrent Inspector of Jiangzhou, and credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he replaced Wen Qiao as general Who Pacifies the South, governor of Jiangzhou military affairs, inspector of the province, and bearer of the credential staff.

sentences.zh: 胤位任轉高，矜豪日甚，縱酒耽樂，不恤政事，大殖財貨，商販百萬。

translations.literal: As Yin's rank and duties rose higher, his arrogance grew daily; he gave himself to wine and pleasure, neglected government, amassed vast wealth, and traded goods worth millions.
translations.idiomatic: Power went to Liu Yin's head: he drank and reveled, ignored administration, hoarded coin, and ran merchant ventures worth millions.

sentences.zh: 初，胤之代嶠也，遠近皆為謂非選。

translations.literal: At first, when Yin succeeded Qiao, those near and far all said it was not the right appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yin first stepped into Wen Qiao's shoes, everyone near and far agreed it was the wrong choice.

sentences.zh: 陶侃、郗鑒咸雲胤非方伯才，朝廷不從。

translations.literal: Tao Kan and Xi Jian both said Yin lacked the talent of a regional governor; the court did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan and Xi Jian both warned that Liu Yin was no provincial governor, yet the court brushed them aside.

sentences.zh: 或問王悅曰：「今大難之後，綱紀弛頓，自江陵至於建康三千餘里，流人萬計，布在江州。

translations.literal: Someone asked Wang Yue: "After this great calamity, laws and discipline are slack; from Jiangling to Jiankang, more than three thousand li, displaced people number in the tens of thousands and are spread across Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A courtier asked Wang Yue: "The realm has barely survived disaster; from Jiangling to Jiankang—over three thousand li—discipline is frayed and tens of thousands of refugees blanket Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 江州，國之南籓，要害之地，而胤以侈忲之性，臥而對之，不有外變，必有內患。

translations.literal: Jiangzhou is the southern bulwark of the state, a place of vital importance; yet Yin, by nature extravagant and overbearing, lies idle over it—if no external crisis arises, there will surely be internal trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou is the dynasty's southern shield, yet Liu Yin, vain and domineering, lounges over it; even without foreign attack, trouble will brew within.

sentences.zh: 」悅曰：「聞溫平南語家公雲，連得惡夢，思見代者。

translations.literal: " Yue said: "I heard Minister Who Pacifies the South Wen tell my father that he kept having nightmares and wished to see someone replace him.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Yue replied: "Minister Wen told my father he suffered nightmares and wanted a successor.

sentences.zh: 尋雲可用劉胤。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he said Liu Yin could be used.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he named Liu Yin as acceptable.

sentences.zh: 此乃溫意，非家公也。

translations.literal: That was Wen's idea, not my father's.
translations.idiomatic: That was Wen Qiao's notion, not my father's judgment.

sentences.zh: 」是時朝廷空罄，百官無祿，惟資江州運漕。

translations.literal: " At that time the court treasury was empty and officials received no salaries; it depended solely on grain shipments from Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " The treasury was bare and no salary reached the ministers; everyone lived off grain convoys from Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 而胤商旅繼路，以私廢公。

translations.literal: Yet Yin's merchant convoys crowded the roads, putting private profit ahead of public duty.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liu Yin's trading trains clogged the highways and private gain trumped the public good.

sentences.zh: 有司奏免胤官。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized to dismiss Yin from office.
translations.idiomatic: The bureaus memorialized to strip Liu Yin of his post.

sentences.zh: 書始下，而胤為郭默所害，年四十九。

translations.literal: The document had barely been issued when Yin was murdered by Guo Mo; he was forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The edict had scarcely gone out when Guo Mo killed him; Liu Yin was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子赤松嗣，尚南平長公主，位至黃門郎、義興太守。

translations.literal: His son Chisong inherited the title, married the Eldest Princess of Nanping, and rose to Palace Gentleman and Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Chisong succeeded to the title, married the Princess of Nanping, and reached the offices of palace gentleman and administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 桓宣，譙國銍人也。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan was a man of Zhi in the Principality of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan came from Zhi in Qiao commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖詡，義陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xu was Administrator of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huan Xu had served as administrator of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 父弼，冠軍長史。

translations.literal: His father Bi was Chief Clerk to the Champion general.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huan Bi was chief clerk on the staff of the Champion general.

sentences.zh: 宣開濟篤素，為元帝丞相舍人。

translations.literal: Xuan was openhanded, earnest, and plain; he served as a secretary to Emperor Yuan's Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan was generous, steady, and unpretentious, and he became a secretary under Emperor Yuan's chancellor.

sentences.zh: 時塢主張平自稱豫州刺史，樊雅自號譙郡太守，各據一城，眾數千人。

translations.literal: At that time the fort master Zhang Ping styled himself Inspector of Yuzhou and Fan Ya called himself Administrator of the Principality of Qiao; each held one walled town with several thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: The stockade chief Zhang Ping claimed the title of inspector of Yuzhou while Fan Ya styled himself administrator of Qiao; each held a citadel and commanded several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 帝以宣信厚，又與平、雅同州裏，轉宣為參軍，使就平、雅。

translations.literal: The emperor, trusting Xuan's honesty and knowing he shared a homeland with Ping and Ya, transferred Xuan to be an aide and sent him to Ping and Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan trusted Huan Xuan's integrity and their common roots with Zhang Ping and Fan Ya, so he moved Xuan onto staff duty and sent him to treat with the pair.

sentences.zh: 平、雅遣軍主簿隨宣詣丞相府受節度，帝皆加四品將軍，即其所部，使捍禦北方。

translations.literal: Ping and Ya dispatched their army clerks to accompany Xuan to the Chancellor's residence to receive orders; the emperor promoted each to general of the fourth rank over their own troops to shield the north.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ping and Fan Ya sent regimental clerks to escort Huan Xuan to the chancellor's office for orders; the emperor named each a fourth-rank general over his own men to hold the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 南中郎將王含請宣為參軍。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the South Wang Han requested Xuan as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han, general Who Guards the South, asked for Huan Xuan as an aide.

sentences.zh: 頃之，豫州刺史祖逖出屯蘆洲，遣參軍殷乂詣平、雅。

translations.literal: Before long, Inspector of Yuzhou Zu Ti advanced and camped at Luzhou, sending aide Yin Yi to Ping and Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zu Ti, inspector of Yuzhou, advanced to Luzhou and sent his aide Yin Yi to Zhang Ping and Fan Ya.

sentences.zh: 乂意輕平，視其屋，雲當持作馬廄，見大鑊，欲鑄作鐵器。

translations.literal: Yi looked down on Ping; surveying his houses, he said they ought to be turned into stables, and seeing a great cauldron he wished to melt it for iron tools.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yi treated Zhang Ping with contempt, sized up his halls as future horse stalls, and eyed a ritual cauldron as scrap iron.

sentences.zh: 平曰：「此是帝王大鑊，天下定後方當用之，奈何打破！

translations.literal: Ping said: "This is the emperor's great cauldron; only after the realm is settled should it be used—how can you smash it!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ping cried: "That is the imperial cauldron for the day the realm is pacified—how dare you break it!

sentences.zh: 」乂曰：「卿能保頭不？

translations.literal: " Yi said: "Can you even keep your head?
translations.idiomatic: " Yin Yi shot back: "Can you even keep your head?

sentences.zh: 而惜大鑊邪！

translations.literal: And you fret over a great cauldron!
translations.idiomatic: And you worry about a kettle!

sentences.zh: 」平大怒，於坐斬乂，阻兵固守。

translations.literal: " Ping was furious and beheaded Yi at the banquet; then he barred his gates with arms.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Ping flew into a rage, executed Yin Yi at the table, and shut his gates for war.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，逖攻平殺之，而雅據譙城。

translations.literal: After more than a year Ti attacked Ping and killed him, while Ya held Qiao city.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Zu Ti assaulted Zhang Ping and slew him while Fan Ya still held Qiao.

sentences.zh: 逖以力弱，求助於含，含遣宣領兵五百助逖。

translations.literal: Ti, being weak in strength, sought help from Han; Han sent Xuan with five hundred men to aid Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti's forces were thin, so he begged Wang Han for help; Han detached Huan Xuan with five hundred soldiers.

sentences.zh: 逖謂宣曰：「卿先已說平、雅，信義大著於彼。

translations.literal: Ti said to Xuan: "You have already persuaded Ping and Ya; your good faith is famed among them.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti told Huan Xuan: "You already won Zhang Ping and Fan Ya with your word; your honor shines there.

sentences.zh: 今復為我說雅。

translations.literal: Now speak again to Ya for me.
translations.idiomatic: Go speak to Fan Ya again on my behalf.

sentences.zh: 雅若降者，方相擢用，不但免死而已。

translations.literal: If Ya submits, he will be promoted and employed—not merely spared death.
translations.idiomatic: If Fan Ya yields, he will be lifted up and employed, not merely spared execution.

sentences.zh: 」宣復單馬從兩人詣雅，曰：「祖逖方欲平蕩二寇，每何卿為援。

translations.literal: " Xuan again rode alone with two men to Ya and said: "Zu Ti intends to wipe out the two bandits and repeatedly looks to you as reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan Xuan rode again with only two followers and said: "Zu Ti means to crush both rebels and leans on you again and again as his ally.

sentences.zh: 前殷乂輕薄，非豫州意。

translations.literal: Earlier Yin Yi was rude and shallow; that was not the Inspector's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yi's insults were his alone; they were not Zu Ti's wish.

sentences.zh: 今若和解，則忠勳可立，富貴可保。

translations.literal: If you reconcile now, loyal merit can be established and honor and wealth preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Make peace now and you can win lasting merit and keep rank and riches.

sentences.zh: 若猶固執，東府赫然更遣猛將，以卿烏合之眾，憑阻窮城，強賊伺其北，國家攻其南，萬無一全也。

translations.literal: If you still stubbornly resist, the eastern headquarters will surely send fierce generals in wrath—with your mob crowding a ruined town, strong bandits watching from the north and the state striking from the south, not one in ten thousand would survive.
translations.idiomatic: If you cling to defiance, the eastern command will answer with seasoned generals; trapped in a broken wall with raiders to your north and imperial troops to your south, almost none of you would survive.

sentences.zh: 願善量之。

translations.literal: I urge you to weigh this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Think it through carefully.

sentences.zh: 」雅與宣置酒結友，遣子隨宣詣逖。

translations.literal: " Ya feasted with Xuan and sealed friendship, then sent his son with Xuan to Zu Ti.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Ya drank with Huan Xuan, pledged friendship, and sent his son back with him to Zu Ti.

sentences.zh: 少日，雅便自詣逖，逖遣雅還撫其眾。

translations.literal: Within days Ya went himself to Ti; Ti sent Ya back to reassure his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Fan Ya presented himself to Zu Ti, who sent him home to steady his troops.

sentences.zh: 雅僉謂前數罵辱，懼罪不敢降。

translations.literal: Ya altogether considered how he had repeatedly reviled them earlier and feared punishment, so he dared not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ya remembered how often he had abused them and feared reprisal, so he hesitated to yield.

sentences.zh: 雅復閉城自守。

translations.literal: Ya closed the city again and held out.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ya slammed the gates shut once more.

sentences.zh: 逖往攻之，復遣宣入說雅。

translations.literal: Ti attacked him and again sent Xuan inside to persuade Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti besieged him and again slipped Huan Xuan inside to argue the point.

sentences.zh: 雅即斬異己者，遂出降。

translations.literal: Ya immediately executed dissenters and then came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ya killed the doubters among his officers and marched out to capitulate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，石勒別將圍譙城，含又遣宣率眾救逖，未至而賊退。

translations.literal: Before long, Shi Le's detached commander besieged Qiao city; Han again sent Xuan with troops to rescue Ti, but the bandits withdrew before they arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Soon one of Shi Le's lieutenants surrounded Qiao; Wang Han again ordered Huan Xuan forward, though the raiders melted away before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 逖留宣討諸未服，皆破之。

translations.literal: Ti kept Xuan to subdue those still unsubmissive; Xuan broke them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti retained Huan Xuan to mop up holdouts, and he shattered every pocket of resistance.

sentences.zh: 遷譙國內史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Interior Secretary of the Principality of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to interior secretary of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 祖約之棄譙城也，宣以箋諫，不從，由是石勒遂有陳留。

translations.literal: When Zu Yue abandoned Qiao city, Xuan remonstrated by letter; Yue did not listen, whereupon Shi Le gained Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Yue quit Qiao, Huan Xuan wrote to dissuade him; Yue refused, and Shi Le seized Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 及約與蘇峻同反，宣謂祖智曰：「今強胡未滅，將戮力以討之，而與峻俱反，此安得久乎！

translations.literal: When Yue joined Su Jun in rebellion, Xuan said to Zu Zhi: "The fierce Hu are not yet destroyed; we ought to combine strength to strike them—yet you rebel alongside Jun; how can that last!
translations.idiomatic: After Zu Yue sided with Su Jun, Huan Xuan warned Zu Zhi: "The northern tribes still threaten us—we should unite against them, yet you rise with Su Jun; how long can that endure?

sentences.zh: 使君若欲為雄霸，何不助國討峻，威名自舉。

translations.literal: If you, sir, wish to play the warlord, why not aid the state in attacking Jun and raise your own renown?
translations.idiomatic: If you crave dominance, why not help the court crush Su Jun and earn fame in the bargain?

sentences.zh: 」智等不能用。

translations.literal: " Zhi and the others would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zu Zhi and his circle ignored him.

sentences.zh: 宣欲諫約，遣其子戎白約求入。

translations.literal: Xuan wished to remonstrate with Yue and sent his son Rong to tell Yue he sought entry.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan meant to confront Zu Yue directly and sent his son Huan Rong to ask leave to enter camp.

sentences.zh: 約知宣必諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Yue knew Xuan would surely remonstrate and refused to hear him.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue knew Huan Xuan would lecture him and barred the gate.

sentences.zh: 宣遂距約，不與之同。

translations.literal: Xuan therefore resisted Yue and would not join him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan therefore opposed Zu Yue and refused the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 邵陵人陳光率部落數百家降宣，宣皆慰撫之。

translations.literal: Chen Guang of Shaoling led several hundred clan households to surrender to Xuan; Xuan comforted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guang of Shaoling brought hundreds of clan families over to Huan Xuan, who welcomed and settled them.

sentences.zh: 約還曆陽，宣將數千家欲南投尋陽，營於馬頭山。

translations.literal: Yue returned to Liyang; Xuan led several thousand families intending to flee south to Xunyang and camped at Mount Matou.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue withdrew to Liyang while Huan Xuan guided several thousand households toward Xunyang and pitched camp at Mount Matou.

sentences.zh: 值祖煥欲襲湓口，陶侃使毛寶救之。

translations.literal: It happened that Zu Huan meant to raid Yikou; Tao Kan sent Mao Bao to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Huan chose that moment to strike Yikou, so Tao Kan dispatched Mao Bao to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 煥遣眾攻宣，宣使戎求救於寶。

translations.literal: Zu Huan sent troops to attack Xuan; Xuan had Rong seek aid from Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Huan assaulted Huan Xuan, who sent Huan Rong to beg Mao Bao for rescue.

sentences.zh: 寶擊煥，破之，宣因投溫嶠。

translations.literal: Bao struck Zu Huan and defeated him; Xuan therefore joined Wen Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao smashed Zu Huan's force, after which Huan Xuan threw in with Wen Qiao.

sentences.zh: 嶠以戎為參軍。

translations.literal: Qiao appointed Rong as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao named Huan Rong his aide.

sentences.zh: 賊平，宣居於武昌，戎復為劉胤參軍。

translations.literal: After the rebels were crushed, Xuan dwelt at Wuchang; Rong again became Liu Yin's aide.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion ended Huan Xuan stayed at Wuchang; Huan Rong later served Liu Yin as aide.

sentences.zh: 郭默害胤，復以戎為參軍。

translations.literal: When Guo Mo murdered Yin, he again took Rong as aide.
translations.idiomatic: After Guo Mo assassinated Liu Yin he pressed Huan Rong back into service.

sentences.zh: 陶侃討默，默遣戎求救于宣，宣偽許之。

translations.literal: When Tao Kan attacked Mo, Mo sent Rong to beg rescue from Xuan; Xuan falsely promised help.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan's expedition against Guo Mo prompted Mo to send Huan Rong to plead with Huan Xuan, who promised aid he never meant to give.

sentences.zh: 西陽太守鄧岳、武昌太守劉詡皆疑宣與默同。

translations.literal: Administrator of Xiyang Deng Yue and Administrator of Wuchang Liu Xu both suspected Xuan of siding with Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yue of Xiyang and Liu Xu of Wuchang suspected Huan Xuan of colluding with Guo Mo.

sentences.zh: 豫州西曹王隨曰：「宣尚背祖約，何緣同郭默邪！

translations.literal: Western Bureau clerk Wang Sui of Yuzhou said: "Xuan once turned against Zu Yue—why would he align with Guo Mo!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui, a western bureau clerk at Yuzhou, argued: "Huan Xuan already broke with Zu Yue—why would he now back Guo Mo?

sentences.zh: 」嶽、詡乃遣隨詣宣以觀之。

translations.literal: " Yue and Xu therefore sent Sui to Xuan to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: " Deng Yue and Liu Xu therefore dispatched Wang Sui to watch Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 隨謂宣曰：「明府心雖不爾，無以自明，惟有以戎付隨耳。

translations.literal: Sui said to Xuan: "Though your heart is not so, you cannot prove it yourself—your only course is to hand Rong over to me.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui told him: "Even if your heart is clean, you cannot prove it—give me Huan Rong if you want trust.

sentences.zh: 」宣乃遣戎與隨俱迎陶侃。

translations.literal: " Xuan then sent Rong with Sui together to welcome Tao Kan.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan Xuan released Huan Rong to accompany Wang Sui to Tao Kan.

sentences.zh: 辟戎為掾，上宣為武昌太守。

translations.literal: Kan recruited Rong as an aide and memorialized Xuan as Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan enrolled Huan Rong as aide and memorialized Huan Xuan as administrator of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 尋遷監沔中軍事、南中郎將、江夏相。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to supervise military affairs on the Han River, General Who Guards the Center of the South, Chancellor of Jiangxia, as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he supervised Han River defenses as general of the southern central court and chancellor of Jiangxia while keeping his former rank.

sentences.zh: 石勒荊州刺史郭敬戍襄陽。

translations.literal: Shi Le's Inspector of Jingzhou, Guo Jing, garrisoned Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing, whom Shi Le had named inspector of Jingzhou, held Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 陶侃使其子平西參軍斌與宣俱攻樊城，拔之。

translations.literal: Tao Kan sent his son Bin, aide to the general Who Pacifies the West, to attack Fancheng jointly with Xuan and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan sent his son Tao Bin, aide to the general Who Pacifies the West, to join Huan Xuan against Fancheng; they captured it.

sentences.zh: 竟陵太守李陽又破新野。

translations.literal: Administrator of Jingling Li Yang again defeated them at Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yang, administrator of Jingling, routed the enemy again at Xinye.

sentences.zh: 敬懼，遁走。

translations.literal: Jing feared this and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing panicked and ran.

sentences.zh: 宣與陽遂平襄陽，侃使宣鎮之，以其淮南部曲立義成郡。

translations.literal: Xuan and Yang thereupon pacified Xiangyang; Kan ordered Xuan to hold it and established Yicheng Commandery from his Huai-nan personal corps.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan and Li Yang secured Xiangyang; Tao Kan told Huan Xuan to stay as commander and carved Yicheng commandery from his Huai River veterans.

sentences.zh: 宣招懷初附，勸課農桑，簡刑罰，略威儀，或載鋤耒於軺軒，或親芸獲於隴畝。

translations.literal: Xuan summoned and soothed the newly attached, urged farming and sericulture, simplified punishments, relaxed ceremony—sometimes carrying hoes and plows in his light carriage, sometimes harvesting with his own hands in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: He soothed new subjects, pushed farming and silk culture, eased penalties, dropped pomp—sometimes hauling hoes in his coach, sometimes reaping beside peasants.

sentences.zh: 十餘年間，石季龍再遣騎攻之，宣能得眾心，每以寡弱距守，論者以為次於祖逖、周訪。

translations.literal: Within a dozen years Shi Jilong twice sent cavalry against him; Xuan won the people's hearts and each time repelled far stronger foes with scant forces—critics ranked him second only to Zu Ti and Zhou Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Across ten years Shi Jilong hurled two cavalry campaigns at him; Huan Xuan kept popular devotion and turned back superior numbers—commentators placed him just below Zu Ti and Zhou Fang.

sentences.zh: 侃方欲使宣北事中原，會侃薨。

translations.literal: Kan had intended to send Xuan north to serve in the Central Plains when Kan died.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan had planned to thrust Huan Xuan toward the Central Plains but died first.

sentences.zh: 後庾亮為荊州，將謀北伐，以宣為都督沔北前鋒征討軍事、平北將軍、司州刺史、假節，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Later Yu Liang held Jingzhou and planned a northern expedition; he appointed Xuan commander of the forward strike north of the Han, general Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Sizhou with credential staff, garrisoning Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang later governed Jingzhou and aimed north, naming Huan Xuan forward commander beyond the Han, general Who Pacifies the North, inspector of Sizhou with credential staff, stationed at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 季龍使騎七千渡沔攻之，亮遣司馬王愆期、輔國將軍毛寶救宣。

translations.literal: Jilong sent seven thousand horsemen across the Han to attack him; Liang sent aide Wang Yanqi and general Who Supports the State Mao Bao to rescue Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong sent seven thousand riders across the Han; Yu Liang answered with Wang Yanqi and Mao Bao, general Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 賊三面為地窟攻城，宣募精勇，出其不意，殺傷數百，多獲鎧馬，賊解圍退走。

translations.literal: The bandits dug tunnels on three sides to storm the city; Xuan recruited crack fighters, struck where they did not expect, killed and wounded several hundred, captured many armored horses, and the bandits lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies tunneled from three faces; Huan Xuan drafted daring troops, ambushed them, killed hundreds, seized armored horses, and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 久之，宣遣步騎收南陽諸郡百姓沒賊者八千餘人以歸。

translations.literal: After a long while Xuan sent infantry and cavalry to recover more than eight thousand commoners of the southern commanderies who had fallen to bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Later he marched foot and horse to rescue over eight thousand southerners trapped under enemy rule.

sentences.zh: 庾翼代亮，欲傾國北討，更以宣為都督司梁雍三州荊州之南陽襄陽新野南鄉四郡軍事、梁州刺史、持節，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Yu Yi succeeded Liang and wished to commit the whole realm to a northern campaign; he reassigned Xuan as commander of military affairs over Si, Liang, and Yong and over four Jiangzhou commanderies—Nanyang, Xiangyang, Xinye, and Nanxiang—with concurrent appointment as Inspector of Liangzhou, holding his generalship as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi replaced Yu Liang and meant to stake the kingdom on a northern war; he gave Huan Xuan command over Si, Liang, Yong, and four Jiangzhou counties—Nanyang, Xiangyang, Xinye, Nanxiang—plus the inspectorate of Liangzhou while keeping his old general's commission.

sentences.zh: 以前後功，封竟陵縣男。

translations.literal: For successive merits he was enfeoffed as Baron of Jingling County.
translations.idiomatic: Cumulative merit won him the barony of Jingling county.

sentences.zh: 宣久在襄陽，綏撫僑舊，甚有稱績。

translations.literal: Xuan long stayed at Xiangyang, comforting settlers old and new, and earned high praise.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan remained years at Xiangyang, steadying native and refugee households alike, and won wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 庾翼遷鎮襄陽，令宣進伐石季龍將李羆，軍次丹水，為賊所敗。

translations.literal: When Yu Yi shifted his headquarters to Xiangyang, he ordered Xuan to advance and attack Shi Jilong's commander Li Pi; the army halted at Danshui and was defeated by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yi moved his seat to Xiangyang he told Huan Xuan to strike Shi Jilong's general Li Pi; the column stopped at Danshui and lost to enemy troops.

sentences.zh: 翼怒，貶宣為建威將軍，使移戍峴山。

translations.literal: Yi was furious, demoted Xuan to general Who Displays Might, and ordered him to shift his garrison to Mount Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi, incensed, stripped Huan Xuan down to general Who Displays Might and reassigned him to guard Mount Xian.

sentences.zh: 宣望實俱喪，兼以老疾，時南蠻校尉王愆期守江陵，以疾求代，翼以宣為鎮南將軍、南郡太守，代愆期。

translations.literal: Xuan had lost both reputation and substance, compounded by age and illness; Colonel Who Subdues the Southern Barbarians Wang Yanqi held Jiangling and requested replacement on grounds of illness, so Yi appointed Xuan general Who Guards the South and Administrator of Nan Commandery in Yanqi's stead.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of prestige and vigor and slowed by age and sickness, Huan Xuan faced relief when Wang Yanqi, colonel on the southern frontier, begged out of Jiangling; Yu Yi named Huan Xuan general Who Guards the South and administrator of Nan commandery to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 宣不得志，未之官，發憤卒。

translations.literal: Xuan, frustrated in ambition, never took office and died of bitter resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan never assumed the post, heartsick and furious, and died before taking command.

sentences.zh: 追贈鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as general Who Guards the South.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously promoted him to general Who Guards the South.

sentences.zh: 戎官至新野太守。

translations.literal: Rong rose to the rank of Administrator of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Rong eventually served as administrator of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 族子伊

translations.literal: Clansman Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His collateral kinsman Huan Yi.

sentences.zh: 伊字叔夏，父景，有當世才幹，仕至侍中、丹陽尹、中領軍、護軍將軍、長社侯，伊有武幹，標悟簡率，為王濛、劉惔所知，頻參諸府軍事，累遷大司馬參軍。

translations.literal: Yi styled Shuxia; his father Jing possessed timely administrative talent and reached Palace Attendant, Administrator of Danyang, Central Army Commander, general Who Guards the Army, and Marquis of Changshe; Yi had martial capacity and was marked by keen insight and straightforward simplicity; Wang Meng and Liu Tan appreciated him; he repeatedly joined headquarters on military affairs and was promoted to aide on the Grand Marshal's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi, courtesy Shuxia, inherited his father Jing's capable service—court posts through marquis of Changshe—and showed martial grit, sharp perception, and blunt simplicity that won Wang Meng and Liu Tan; staff appointments piled up until he served the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 時苻堅強盛，邊鄙多虞，朝議選能距捍疆場者，乃授伊淮南太守。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Jian was powerful and the frontier bristled with alarms; court deliberation chose someone able to hold the marches and appointed Yi Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's might kept the borders uneasy, so ministers picked Huan Yi to hold the line as administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 以綏禦有方，進督豫州之十二郡揚州之江西五郡軍事、建威將軍、曆陽太守，淮南如故。

translations.literal: Because he soothed and defended effectively, he was advanced to supervise military affairs over twelve commanderies of Yuzhou and five commanderies west of the river in Yangzhou, became general Who Displays Might and Administrator of Liyang, retaining Huainan as before.
translations.idiomatic: His steady hand on defense earned him command over a dozen Yuzhou counties plus five Yangzhou counties west of the Long River, the generalship Who Displays Might, and the Liyang magistracy while he kept Huainan.

sentences.zh: 與謝玄共破賊別將王鑒、張蠔等，以功封宣城縣子，又進都督豫州諸軍事、西中郎將、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Together with Xie Xuan he defeated the bandits' detached commanders Wang Jian and Zhang Hao and others; for merit he was enfeoffed Viscount of Xuancheng and further promoted commander of all military affairs of Yuzhou, General of the Western Palace Court, and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Xie Xuan he crushed Wang Jian, Zhang Hao, and other enemy columns, meriting the viscounty of Xuancheng and later full Yuzhou command as western palace general and inspector.

sentences.zh: 及苻堅南寇，伊與冠軍將軍謝玄、輔國將軍謝琰俱破堅於肥水，以功封永修縣侯，進號右軍將軍，賜錢百萬，袍表千端。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian invaded south, Yi together with Champion general Xie Xuan and general Who Supports the State Xie Yan defeated Jian at the Fei River; for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yongxiu, promoted to general of the Right Army, and granted a million cash and a thousand bolts of robe silk.
translations.idiomatic: At the Fei River he stood with Xie Xuan and Xie Yan to break Fu Jian's southern thrust, earning the marquisate of Yongxiu, the title of general of the Right Army, and lavish gifts of coin and silk.

sentences.zh: 伊性謙素，雖有大功，而始終不替。

translations.literal: Yi was modest by nature; though he achieved great merit, he never changed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi stayed humble even after towering deeds and never put on airs.

sentences.zh: 善音樂，盡一時之妙，為江左第一。

translations.literal: He excelled at music and attained the utmost mastery of his age, ranking first east of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: In musicianship he matched the finest of the age and stood first among talent east of the river.

sentences.zh: 有蔡邕柯亭笛，常自吹之。

translations.literal: He possessed Cai Yong's Ke Pavilion flute and often played it himself.
translations.idiomatic: He kept Cai Yong's flute from Ke Pavilion and often performed on it.

sentences.zh: 王徽之赴召京師，泊舟青溪側。

translations.literal: Wang Huizhi went to the capital on summons and moored his boat beside the Green Creek.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the capital, Wang Huizhi tied up below Green Creek.

sentences.zh: 素不與徽之相識。

translations.literal: He had never been acquainted with Huizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi had never met Wang Huizhi before.

sentences.zh: 伊於岸上過，船中客稱伊小字曰：「此桓野王也。

translations.literal: Yi passed along the bank; a passenger in the boat called Yi's childhood name and said: "That is Huan the Wild Lord.
translations.idiomatic: As Huan Yi walked the shore a traveler in the boat cried his childhood name: "There goes Wild Lord Huan.

sentences.zh: 」徽之便令人謂伊曰：「聞君善吹笛，試為我一奏。

translations.literal: " Huizhi then sent someone to tell Yi: "I hear you play the flute well—play a piece for me.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Huizhi sent word: "They say your flute is unmatched—play for me.

sentences.zh: 」伊是時已貴顯，素聞徽之名，便下車，踞胡床，為作三調，弄畢，便上車去，客主不交一言。

translations.literal: " Though Yi was already eminent and had long heard Huizhi's name, he stepped from his carriage, sat cross-legged on a folding stool, performed three tunes, finished his improvisation, boarded his carriage and left—host and guest exchanged not a word.
translations.idiomatic: " Already a great man who respected Wang Huizhi's fame, Huan Yi still dismounted, spread a camp stool, ripped through three pieces, remounted, and rode off—not a sentence passed between them.

sentences.zh: 時謝安女婿王國寶專利無檢行，安惡其為人，每抑制之。

translations.literal: At that time Xie An's son-in-law Wang Guobao behaved graspingly without restraint; An detested his character and constantly restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guobao, Xie An's son-in-law, grew rich through shameless grabs; Xie An despised him and checked him at every turn.

sentences.zh: 及孝武末年，嗜酒好內，而會稽王道子昏ＪＴ尤甚，惟狎昵諂邪，於是國寶讒諛之計稍行於主相之間。

translations.literal: By the late Xiaowu reign the emperor indulged wine and inner chambers, while Prince of Kuaiji Wang Daozi sank deeper into befuddled dissipation; he favored only flatterers and sycophants, so Guobao's slanderous schemes gradually operated between sovereign and chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Xiaowu's reign the throne drowned in wine and harem sport while Prince Wang Daozi of Kuaiji slid deeper into folly and vice, cuddling only sneaks and toadies—room for Wang Guobao's whisper campaigns between emperor and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 而好利險詖之徒，以安功名盛極，而構會之，嫌隙遂成。

translations.literal: Men greedy and treacherous, seeing An's fame at its peak, engineered suspicion against him, and estrangement took shape.
translations.idiomatic: The grasping and crooked, jealous of Xie An's zenith, spun plots until sovereign and minister eyed each other with mistrust.

sentences.zh: 帝召伊飲宴，安侍坐。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Yi to a drinking banquet with An in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Huan Yi to drink while Xie An sat with them.

sentences.zh: 帝命伊吹笛。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yi to play the flute.
translations.idiomatic: He told Huan Yi to sound the flute.

sentences.zh: 伊神色無迕，即吹為一弄，乃放笛云：「臣於箏分乃不及笛，然自足以韻合歌管，請以箏歌，並請一吹笛人。

translations.literal: Yi showed no awkwardness, played one suite at once, then set down the flute and said: "In skill on the zheng I do not match the flute, yet it is enough to harmonize with song and pipes—allow me to sing to the zheng and also request one flutist.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi betrayed no unease, delivered a full set, laid the flute aside, and said: "My zheng falls short of my piping, yet it can carry a song—let me sing with it and borrow another blower.

sentences.zh: 」帝善其調達，乃敕禦妓奏笛。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised his tact and ordered palace musicians to play flute.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor admired his poise and told court musicians to answer on flute.

sentences.zh: 伊又云：「禦府人於臣必自不合，臣有一奴，善相便串。

translations.literal: Yi added: "Palace performers would surely not suit me; I have a slave skilled at accompanying.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Your palace band would clash with me—I keep a servant who blends well.

sentences.zh: 」帝彌賞其放率，乃許召之。

translations.literal: " The emperor all the more admired his candor and permitted summoning him.
translations.idiomatic: " Delighted by his blunt honesty, the emperor let him call the man in.

sentences.zh: 奴既吹笛，伊便撫箏而歌《怨詩》曰：「為君既不易，為臣良獨難。

translations.literal: When the slave had played the flute, Yi plucked the zheng and sang 《Song of Resentment》: "To be your lord is already hard; to be your minister is harder still.
translations.idiomatic: After the slave piped, Huan Yi struck the zheng and sang 《Song of Resentment》: "Serving as lord is never easy; serving as minister is harder still.

sentences.zh: 忠信事不顯，乃有見疑患。

translations.literal: Loyalty goes unseen; then comes suspicion's plague.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal faith wins no spotlight—only doubt crowds in.

sentences.zh: 周旦佐文武，《金縢》功不刊。

translations.literal: The Zhou dukes aided kings Wen and Wu; 《Metal-bound Coffer》 records deeds never to be erased.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou dukes steadied King Wen and King Wu; 《Metal-bound Coffer》 preserves their uncarved merit.

sentences.zh: 推心輔王政，二叔反流言。

translations.literal: With open hearts they aided the royal government; the two uncles spread slanderous rumor.
translations.idiomatic: They lent whole hearts to the throne—yet the two rival uncles aired poisonous gossip.

sentences.zh: 」聲節慷慨，俯仰可觀。

translations.literal: " His tones were stirring in rhythm and gesture.
translations.idiomatic: " Every phrase rang with fierce cadence; his bearing matched the words.

sentences.zh: 安泣下沾衿，乃越席而就之，捋其須曰：「使君于此不凡！

translations.literal: An wept until his collar was soaked; crossing his mat he approached Yi, stroked his beard and said: "You are no ordinary man in this!
translations.idiomatic: Xie An wept until his collar ran wet, slid across the mat, tugged Huan Yi's beard, and cried: "No ordinary soul could do this!

sentences.zh: 」帝甚有愧色。

translations.literal: " The emperor looked deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 伊在州十年，綏撫荒雜，甚得物情。

translations.literal: Yi held the province ten years, comforting a mixed and desolate population, and won great sympathy.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi governed a decade, steadying a battered, mixed populace and earning deep affection.

sentences.zh: 桓沖卒，遷都督江州荊州十郡豫州四郡軍事、江州刺史，將軍如故，假節。

translations.literal: When Huan Chong died, Yi was transferred to commander of military affairs over ten commanderies of Jiangzhou and Jingzhou and four of Yuzhou, Inspector of Jiangzhou, general as before, with credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Chong's death he took joint command of Jiangzhou, Jingzhou, and four Yuzhou counties, kept his general's commission, bore the credential staff, and became inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 伊到鎮，以邊境無虞，宜以寬恤為務，乃上疏以江州虛秏，加連歲不登，今餘戶有五萬六千，宜併合小縣，除諸郡逋米，移州還鎮豫章。

translations.literal: When Yi reached his post, deeming the frontier quiet and relief the proper task, he memorialized that Jiangzhou was drained and harvests had failed year after year; the remaining households numbered fifty-six thousand and ought to merge petty counties, remit overdue grain owed commanderies, and move the provincial seat back to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he judged the border calm and pushed lenient relief, arguing that Jiangzhou was bled white by serial crop failure—only fifty-six thousand households remained—so petty counties should merge, grain arrears should vanish, and the provincial seat should return to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 詔令移州尋陽，其餘皆聽之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the province shifted to Xunyang; the rest was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne shifted the provincial seat to Xunyang and granted the other requests.

sentences.zh: 伊隨宜拯撫，百姓賴焉。

translations.literal: Yi aided and settled as circumstances demanded; the people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: He patched wounds wherever needed and the people leaned on him.

sentences.zh: 在任累年，徵拜護軍將軍。

translations.literal: After many years in office he was summoned as general Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Years later the court recalled him as general Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 以右軍府千人自隨，配護軍府。

translations.literal: He brought the thousand men of the Right Army headquarters with him to staff the Guard Army office.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred the thousand household guards of the Right Army headquarters into the Guard Army staff.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died still holding office.

sentences.zh: 贈右將軍，加散騎常侍，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as general of the Right with additional appointment as palace attendant cavalier in ordinary attendance; posthumous title Martyr.
translations.idiomatic: They posthumously named him general of the right, added ordinary attendant status, and gave the posthumous epithet Martyr.

sentences.zh: 初，伊有馬步鎧六百領，豫為表，令死乃上之。

translations.literal: At first Yi had six hundred suits of horse and foot armor; he prepared a memorial in advance ordering it submitted only after his death.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Huan Yi stockpiled six hundred suits of horse and foot mail and drafted a memorial to file only after his death.

sentences.zh: 表曰：「臣過蒙殊寵，受任西籓。

translations.literal: The memorial said: "I have received undue favor and hold the western march.
translations.idiomatic: It read: "Beyond merit I was favored with the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 淮南之捷，逆兵奔北，人馬器鎧，隨處放散。

translations.literal: At the Huainan victory the rebel army fled north; men, horses, and armor were scattered everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan fell the foe fled north, littering the roads with men, mounts, and harness.

sentences.zh: 于時收拾敗破，不足貫連。

translations.literal: At that time we gathered broken gear—too little to string together.
translations.idiomatic: What we salvaged then was scraps—barely enough to equip a line.

sentences.zh: 比年營繕，並已修整。

translations.literal: Over the years camp workshops have restored it all.
translations.idiomatic: Workshops since patched every piece.

sentences.zh: 今六合雖一，餘燼未滅，臣不以朽邁，猶欲輸效力命，仰報皇恩。

translations.literal: Though the realm is now united, embers of rebellion remain; though I am old and worn, I still wished to offer my strength and repay imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: The realm looks whole yet sparks remain; though I am aged and frail I hoped still to spend my strength repaying the throne.

sentences.zh: 此志永絕，銜恨泉壤。

translations.literal: That resolve is ended forever; I bear regret unto the yellow springs.
translations.idiomatic: That dream is ended—I carry regret into the grave.

sentences.zh: 謹奉輸馬具裝百具、步鎧五百領，並在尋陽，請勒所屬領受。

translations.literal: I respectfully present one hundred fully barded horses, five hundred suits of foot armor, stored at Xunyang—order the relevant offices to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: I deliver one hundred caparisoned mounts and five hundred suits of infantry armor held at Xunyang—please tell the bureaus to take charge.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「伊忠誠不遂，益以傷懷，仍受其所上之鎧。」

translations.literal: " The edict said: "Yi's loyalty unfulfilled wounds us the more; accept the armor he presents."
translations.idiomatic: " The edict answered: "Huan Yi's devotion cut short deepens our grief—take the armor he offers."

sentences.zh: 子肅之嗣。

translations.literal: His son Suzhi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Suzhi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 卒，子陵嗣。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Ling inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzhi died, Ling inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Song received the abdication, the principality was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu Song takeover erased the fief.

sentences.zh: 伊弟不才，亦有將略。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Bucai also possessed strategic talent.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Huan Bucai too carried tactical skill.

sentences.zh: 討孫恩，至冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He campaigned against Sun En and reached the rank of Champion general.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Sun En he rose to champion general.

sentences.zh: 硃伺，字仲文，安陸人。

translations.literal: Zhu Si, styled Zhongwen, was a man of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Si, courtesy Zhongwen, came from Anlu.

sentences.zh: 少為吳牙門將陶丹給使。

translations.literal: In youth he served as orderly for Wu's garrison commander Tao Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he was a runner for Tao Dan, Wu's camp commander.

sentences.zh: 吳平，內徙江夏。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, he was moved inland to Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wu's fall brought him resettled in Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 伺有武勇，而訥口，不知書，為郡將督，見鄉里士大夫，揖稱名而已。

translations.literal: Si was martially brave but tongue-tied and illiterate; as commandery captain he merely bowed and spoke his name when meeting local gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Brave but halting and unread, he served as county captain and only bowed and announced his name before local scholars.

sentences.zh: 及為將，遂以謙恭稱。

translations.literal: Once he became a commander, he was praised for modesty.
translations.idiomatic: Once promoted to general he won praise for humility.

sentences.zh: 張昌之逆，太守弓欽走灄口，伺與同輩郴寶、布興合眾討之，不克，乃與欽奔武昌。

translations.literal: During Zhang Chang's rebellion the Administrator Gong Qin fled to Hankou; Si joined peers Chen Bao and Bu Xing to raise troops against him; failing, he fled with Qin to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chang rose, Administrator Gong Qin bolted to Hankou; Zhu Si with Chen Bao and Bu Xing tried to crush the revolt, failed, and ran with Gong Qin to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 後更率部黨攻滅之。

translations.literal: Later he led his clique to attack and destroy Zhang Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he rallied his band and wiped Zhang Chang out.

sentences.zh: 轉騎部曲督，加綏夷都尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to cavalry corps commander with additional appointment as colonel Who Pacifies the Yi.
translations.idiomatic: They moved him to cavalry corps command and named him colonel Who Pacifies the Yi.

sentences.zh: 伺部曲等以諸縣附昌，惟本部唱義討逆，逆順有嫌，求別立縣，因此遂割安陸東界為灄陽縣而貫焉。

translations.literal: Si's troops noted that various counties had sided with Zhang Chang while only their corps had raised the righteous cause against the rebel—the awkwardness of opposing former neighbors led them to ask for a separate county; accordingly the eastern border of Anlu was carved off as Sheyang County and attached to them.
translations.idiomatic: His soldiers noted neighbors had backed Zhang Chang while they alone struck the traitor—awkward living among former allies—so they won a new county carved from eastern Anlu called Sheyang.

sentences.zh: 其後陳敏作亂，陶侃時鎮江夏，以伺能水戰，曉作舟艦，乃遣作大艦，署為左甄，據江口，摧破敏前鋒。

translations.literal: Later Chen Min rebelled; Tao Kan then held Jiangxia and, knowing Si excelled at river combat and understood building ships, sent him to construct a great vessel, appointed him left horn of the formation, held the river mouth, and shattered Chen Min's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min's revolt found Tao Kan defending Jiangxia; knowing Zhu Si mastered river war and shipwrighting, Kan built a great hull, posted him on the left horn at the estuary, and shattered Chen Min's van.

sentences.zh: 敏弟恢稱荊州刺史，在武昌，侃率伺及諸軍進討，破之。

translations.literal: Min's younger brother Hui styled himself Inspector of Jingzhou at Wuchang; Kan led Si and the host to attack and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min's brother Hui claimed Jingzhou from Wuchang until Tao Kan marched Zhu Si and the army to break him.

sentences.zh: 敏、恢既平，伺以功封亭侯，領騎督。

translations.literal: After Min and Hui were pacified, Si was enfeoffed Village Marquis for merit and became cavalry commander.
translations.idiomatic: Once both brothers fell Zhu Si earned a village marquisate and cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 時西陽夷賊抄掠江夏，太守楊瑉每請督將議距賊之計，伺獨不言。

translations.literal: At that time Xiyang Yi bandits raided Jiangxia; Administrator Yang Min constantly convened commanders to discuss resisting them; alone Si said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyang tribesmen harried Jiangxia while Administrator Yang Min endlessly convened officers—Zhu Si alone stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 瑉曰：「硃將軍何以不言？

translations.literal: Min said: "Why does General Zhu not speak?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Min asked: "Why nothing from General Zhu?

sentences.zh: 」伺答曰：「諸人以舌擊賊，伺惟以力耳。

translations.literal: " Si replied: "They all strike bandits with tongues; I only strike with strength.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu Si answered: "They fight with words; I fight with steel.

sentences.zh: 」瑉又問：「將軍前後擊賊，何以每得勝邪？

translations.literal: " Min asked again: "General, when you fight bandits why do you always win?
translations.idiomatic: " "Then why do you always win?" Yang pressed.

sentences.zh: 」伺曰：「兩敵共對，惟當忍之。

translations.literal: " Si said: "When two foes face each other, one must endure.
translations.idiomatic: " "Because two armies meet and patience decides it.

sentences.zh: 彼不能忍，我能忍，是以勝耳。

translations.literal: They cannot endure; I can—that is why I win.
translations.idiomatic: They lose patience first; I wait—that is victory.

sentences.zh: 」瑉大笑。

translations.literal: " Min roared with laughter.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Min roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，石勒破江夏，伺與楊瑉走夏口。

translations.literal: During Yongjia, Shi Le crushed Jiangxia; Si and Yang Min fled to Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yongjia reign Shi Le smashed Jiangxia; Zhu Si and Yang Min escaped to Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 及陶侃來戍夏口，伺依之，加明威將軍。

translations.literal: When Tao Kan came to garrison Xiakou, Si attached himself to him and was promoted general Who Displays Martial Glory.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan's arrival at Xiakou drew Zhu Si into his command and the generalship Who Displays Martial Glory.

sentences.zh: 隨侃討杜弢，有殊功，語在侃傳。

translations.literal: He followed Kan against Du Tao with exceptional merit, as related in Kan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Kan against Du Tao with standout feats recorded in Kan's memoir.

sentences.zh: 夏口之戰，伺用鐵面自衛，以弩的射賊大帥數人，皆殺之。

translations.literal: At the battle of Xiakou Si wore an iron mask for protection and with crossbow sights shot several enemy chiefs, killing them.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiakou he wore an iron mask, aimed his crossbow, and dropped several enemy captains.

sentences.zh: 賊挽船上岸，於水邊作陣。

translations.literal: The bandits towed boats ashore and formed ranks along the water.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders dragged boats aground and drew lines along the bank.

sentences.zh: 伺逐水上下以邀之，箭中其脛，氣色不變。

translations.literal: Si ranged up and down the water to intercept them; an arrow struck his shin yet his bearing never changed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Si prowled the shallows to cut them off; a bolt pierced his shin yet his face stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 諸軍尋至，賊潰，追擊之，皆棄船投水，死者太半。

translations.literal: The armies soon arrived; the bandits broke and fled in pursuit; all abandoned boats for the water and more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements arrived, routed them, and drove survivors into the river—more than half drowned.

sentences.zh: 賊夜還長沙，伺追蒲圻，不及而反。

translations.literal: The bandits fled by night to Changsha; Si pursued to Puqi but did not catch them and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: They slipped overnight toward Changsha; Zhu Si chased to Puqi, missed them, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 加威遠將軍，赤幢曲蓋。

translations.literal: He was promoted general Who Displays Far Might with crimson banner and curved canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion followed to general Who Displays Far Might with scarlet banner and curved canopy.

sentences.zh: 建興中，陳聲率諸無賴二千餘家斷江抄掠，侃遣伺為督護討聲。

translations.literal: During Jianxing, Chen Sheng led over two thousand rogue households to block the river and plunder; Kan dispatched Si as protector to attack Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing Chen Sheng stacked two thousand restless families across the river as pirates until Tao Kan sent Zhu Si as protector to crush him.

sentences.zh: 聲眾雖少，伺容之不擊，求遣弟詣侃降，伺外許之。

translations.literal: Though Sheng's followers were few, Si tolerated them without striking and requested permission to send his younger brother to Kan to surrender; Si outwardly consented.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng's band was small yet Zhu Si held fire, let him send a brother to sue for peace with Kan, and nodded along.

sentences.zh: 及聲去，伺乃遣勁勇要聲弟斬之，潛軍襲聲。

translations.literal: After Sheng departed, Si sent crack troops to intercept Sheng's brother and behead him, then secretly marched against Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chen Sheng left, Zhu Si ambushed the brother, took his head, and stole a march on the chief.

sentences.zh: 聲正旦並出祭祀飲食，伺軍入其門方覺。

translations.literal: On New Year's morning Sheng all went out for sacrifice and feasting; Si's troops entered his gate before he noticed.
translations.idiomatic: New Year's dawn found Chen Sheng's men feasting at sacrifice while Zhu Si burst his gates unnoticed.

sentences.zh: 聲將閻晉、鄭進皆死戰，伺軍人多傷，乃還營。

translations.literal: Sheng's commanders Yan Jin and Zheng Jin fought to the death; Si's men suffered many wounds and withdrew to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Captains Yan Jin and Zheng Jin sold their lives dearly; Zhu Si's troops bled heavy losses and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 聲東走，保董城。

translations.literal: Sheng fled east and held Dong City.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng bolted east and dug in at Dong city.

sentences.zh: 伺又率諸軍圍守之，遂重柴繞城，作高櫓，以勁弩下射之，又斷其水道。

translations.literal: Si again led the host to besiege him, piled heavy firewood around the walls, built lofty towers, shot down with powerful crossbows, and cut his water supply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Si invested the place, ringed it with faggots, raised tall racks, poured crossbow fire downward, and dammed the water.

sentences.zh: 城中無水，殺牛飲血。
