translations.literal: With no water inside the city they slaughtered cattle and drank blood.
translations.idiomatic: Dry wells drove them to butcher cattle and drink blood.

sentences.zh: 閻晉，聲婦弟也，乃斬聲首出降。

translations.literal: Yan Jin was Sheng's wife's younger brother; he beheaded Sheng and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jin, Chen Sheng's brother-in-law, struck off his head and walked out to yield.

sentences.zh: 又以平蜀賊襲高之功，加伺廣威將軍，領竟陵內史。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Shu bandit Xi Gao, Si was promoted general Who Displays Broad Might and concurrent Interior Secretary of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Breaking Shu raider Xi Gao earned Zhu Si the generalship Who Displays Broad Might and the interior secretaryship of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 時王敦欲用從弟暠代侃為荊州，侃故將鄭攀、馬俊等乞侃於敦，敦不許。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Dun wished to install his cousin Gao to replace Kan as Inspector of Jingzhou; Kan's old officers Zheng Pan and Ma Jun begged Dun on Kan's behalf but Dun refused.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun meant to swap Tao Kan for cousin Wang Gao as Jingzhou inspector; Kan's veterans Zheng Pan and Ma Jun pleaded in vain.

sentences.zh: 攀等以侃始滅大賊，人皆樂附，又以暠忌戾難事，謀共距之。

translations.literal: Pan and others noted Kan had just destroyed a great bandit and men gladly followed him, also that Gao was jealous and cruel and hard to serve; they plotted jointly to resist.
translations.idiomatic: They argued Tao Kan had just crushed a major foe and kept popular loyalty, whereas Wang Gao was jealous and vicious—so they conspired to resist.

sentences.zh: 遂屯結溳口，遣使告伺。

translations.literal: They massed at Hankou and sent envoys to inform Si.
translations.idiomatic: They rallied at Hankou and messaged Zhu Si.

sentences.zh: 伺外許之，而稱疾不赴。

translations.literal: Si outwardly consented but pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Si agreed in words but pleaded sickness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 攀等遂進距暠。

translations.literal: Pan and others therefore advanced to oppose Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Pan and company then marched against Wang Gao.

sentences.zh: 既而士眾疑阻，復散還橫桑口，欲入杜曾。

translations.literal: Presently the troops hesitated and broke apart, scattered back to Hengsangkou, and intended to join Du Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: Morale collapsed: the host melted away toward Hengsangkou hoping to throw in with Du Zeng.

sentences.zh: 時硃軌、趙誘、李桓率眾將擊之，攀等懼誅，以司馬孫景造謀距暠，因斬之，降軌等。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Gui, Zhao You, and Li Huan led troops to strike them; Pan and others feared execution and, claiming Marshal Sun Jing had plotted resistance against Gao, beheaded him and surrendered to Gui and company.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gui, Zhao You, and Li Huan threw weight against them; fearing the headsman, Zheng Pan blamed staff officer Sun Jing for opposing Wang Gao, cut him down, and yielded to Zhu Gui.

sentences.zh: 廙將西出，遣長史劉浚留鎮揚口壘。

translations.literal: Tao Kan was about to march west and dispatched Chief Clerk Liu Jun to remain and hold the rampart at Yangkou.
translations.idiomatic: Preparing a western advance, Tao Kan left chief clerk Liu Jun to guard the Yangkou stockade.

sentences.zh: 時杜曾會請討第五猗於襄陽，伺謂廙曰：「曾是猾賊，外示西還，以疑眾心，欲誘引官軍使西，然後兼道襲揚口耳。

translations.literal: At that time Du Zeng had offered to attack Di Wuyi at Xiangyang; Si said to Tao Kan: "Zeng is a slippery rogue who feigns heading west to unsettle our ranks—he means to drag imperial troops westward, then double back and hit Yangkou along main and side roads.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng volunteered to strike Di Wuyi at Xiangyang; Zhu Si warned Tao Kan: "Du Zeng is cunning—his westward show is bait to split our minds and lure the army away before he races down on Yangkou.

sentences.zh: 宜大部分，未可便西。

translations.literal: You ought to keep the bulk of the host massed; you must not hurry west yet.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the main body ready—do not march west on impulse.

sentences.zh: 」廙性矜厲自用，兼以伺老怯難信，遂西行。

translations.literal: " Tao Kan was harsh, proud, and self-willed; he also thought Si old, timid, and untrustworthy, and therefore marched west.
translations.idiomatic: " Tao Kan, rigid and sure of himself, discounted Zhu Si as a fearful old man and pushed west anyway.

sentences.zh: 曾等果馳還。

translations.literal: Zeng and others indeed galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng wheeled his riders home exactly as predicted.

sentences.zh: 廙乃遣伺歸，裁至壘，即為曾等所圍。

translations.literal: Tao Kan then sent Si back; barely reaching the fort, Si was surrounded by Zeng and company.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan recalled Zhu Si, who had scarcely reached the fort before Du Zeng ringed it.

sentences.zh: 劉浚以壘北門危，欲令伺守之。

translations.literal: Liu Jun deemed the north gate dangerous and wished to assign Si to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun saw the north gate as the weak point and wanted Zhu Si there.

sentences.zh: 或說浚云：「伺與鄭攀同者。

translations.literal: Someone advised Jun: "Si is of the same party as Zheng Pan.
translations.idiomatic: A whisperer told Liu Jun: "Zhu Si marched with Zheng Pan.

sentences.zh: 」乃轉守南門。

translations.literal: " So he was shifted to guard the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: " So Zhu Si was posted to the south gate instead.

sentences.zh: 賊知之，攻其北門。

translations.literal: The bandits learned of it and assaulted the north gate.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy learned the switch and stormed the north wall.

sentences.zh: 時鄭攀党馬俊等亦來攻壘，俊妻子先在壘內，或請皮其面以示之。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Pan's partisan Ma Jun and others also came to attack the fort; Jun's wife and children were already inside the rampart, and some urged flaying their faces to display to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jun, still tied to Zheng Pan, joined the assault; Liu Jun's family sat inside, and voices called for mutilating them to break his nerve.

sentences.zh: 伺曰：「殺其妻子，未能解圍，但益其怒耳。

translations.literal: Si said: "Killing his wife and children would not lift the siege—it would only deepen his rage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Si answered: "Murdering kin will not open the walls—only fan his fury.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " So they desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " They dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 伺常所調弩忽噤不發，伺甚惡之。

translations.literal: The crossbow Si regularly adjusted suddenly jammed and would not shoot; Si took this as a dire omen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Si's favorite crossbow froze silent—an ill sign he loathed.

sentences.zh: 及賊攻陷北門，伺被傷退入船。

translations.literal: When the bandits breached the north gate, Si was wounded and withdrew into a boat.
translations.idiomatic: The north gate fell; Zhu Si, bleeding, fell back aboard ship.

sentences.zh: 初，浚開諸船底，以木掩之，名為船械。

translations.literal: At first Jun had opened the bottoms of all boats and covered them with planks, calling them "boat traps."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun had bored hull plugs and masked them with boards—his so-called boat traps.

sentences.zh: 伺既入，賊舉鋋摘伺，伺逆接得鋋，反以摘賊。

translations.literal: Once Si had entered, the bandits raised spears to hook him; Si caught the spear point and turned it back against them.
translations.idiomatic: Once aboard they thrust boat-hooks at Zhu Si; he caught the shaft and hooked them in return.

sentences.zh: 賊走上船屋，大喚云：「賊帥在此！

translations.literal: The bandits fled onto the cabin roof and shouted: "The bandit chief is here!
translations.idiomatic: They scrambled to the deckhouse yelling: "The rebel chief is here!

sentences.zh: 」伺從船底沈行五十步，乃免。

translations.literal: " Si submerged along the hull for fifty paces and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu Si slipped underwater fifty paces along the keel and broke free.

sentences.zh: 遇醫療，創小差。

translations.literal: He met doctors; his wounds began to heal.
translations.idiomatic: Surgeons dressed him and the gashes began to close.

sentences.zh: 杜曾遣說伺云：「馬俊等感卿恩，妻孥得活。

translations.literal: Du Zeng sent someone to persuade Si: "Ma Jun and others are grateful for your kindness—his wife and children lived because of you.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng's envoy wheedled: "Ma Jun owes you every breath his family draws.

sentences.zh: 盡以卿家外內百口付俊，俊已盡心收視，卿可來也。

translations.literal: He has placed every mouth—inside and outside—of your household in Jun's care; Jun has sheltered them faithfully—you may come over.
translations.idiomatic: He guards a hundred of your kin—every soul—and tends them honestly; join us.

sentences.zh: 」伺答曰：「賊無白首者，今吾年六十餘，不能復與卿作賊。

translations.literal: " Si answered: "Bandits never die of old age; I am over sixty and will not turn bandit again for you.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu Si replied: "Rebels never see white hair; I am past sixty and will not ride with thieves.

sentences.zh: 吾死，當歸南，妻子付汝。

translations.literal: When I die, I shall return south; my wife and children are yours to keep.
translations.idiomatic: When I fall, send my bones south—keep wife and children if you must.

sentences.zh: 」乃還甑山。

translations.literal: " So he returned to Zeng Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: " He withdrew to Mount Zeng.

sentences.zh: 時王暠與李桓、杜曾相持，累戰甑山下。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Gao locked horns with Li Huan and Du Zeng, fighting repeatedly below Mount Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gao, Li Huan, and Du Zeng traded blows for days beneath Mount Zeng.

sentences.zh: 軍士數驚喚云：「賊欲至！

translations.literal: Soldiers kept screaming: "The bandits are coming!
translations.idiomatic: Men shrieked night and day: "Here they come!

sentences.zh: 」伺驚創而卒。

translations.literal: " Si started at the wound and died.
translations.idiomatic: " The alarm tore Zhu Si's wound open and killed him.

sentences.zh: 因葬甑山。

translations.literal: He was therefore buried on Mount Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: They buried him on Mount Zeng.

sentences.zh: 毛寶，字碩真，滎陽陽武人也。

translations.literal: Mao Bao, styled Shuozhen, was a man of Yangwu in Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao, courtesy Shuozhen, hailed from Yangwu in Yingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 王敦以為臨湘令。

translations.literal: Wang Dun appointed him magistrate of Linxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun named him magistrate of Linxiang.

sentences.zh: 敦卒，為溫嶠平南參軍。

translations.literal: When Dun died, he became an aide on Wen Qiao's staff as general Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun's death he joined Wen Qiao as aide under the general Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻作逆，嶠將赴難，而征西將軍陶侃懷疑不從。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, Qiao prepared to march to the rescue, but general Who Conquers the West Tao Kan hesitated and would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun's revolt drew Wen Qiao toward the capital while Tao Kan, general Who Conquers the West, hung back in doubt.

sentences.zh: 嶠屢說不能回，更遣使順侃意曰：「仁公且守，僕宜先下。

translations.literal: Qiao argued repeatedly without swaying him and finally sent an envoy phrased to suit Kan: "My lord, hold your ground awhile—I should descend first.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao's pleas failed, so he couched a letter to stroke Kan's pride: "Stay put, my lord—I will move downstream first.

sentences.zh: 」遣信已二日，會寶別使還，聞之，說嶠曰：「凡舉大事，當與天下共同，眾克在和，不聞有異。

translations.literal: " The messenger had been gone two days when Bao's separate envoy returned; hearing this, he told Qiao: "Whenever one raises a great affair one must act with the realm at one's side—victory rests in harmony; one never hears of success through division.
translations.idiomatic: " Two days after the courier left, Mao Bao's own rider returned; hearing the plan, he told Wen Qiao: "Great ventures need unity—harmony wins wars; nobody conquers by sowing mistrust.

sentences.zh: 假令可疑，猶當外示不覺，況自作疑耶！

translations.literal: Even if suspicion were warranted, one should outwardly show no sign—how much less stir doubt oneself!
translations.idiomatic: Even if doubt were fair, feign trust—never manufacture suspicion yourself!

sentences.zh: 便宜急追信，改舊書，說必應俱征。

translations.literal: Best hurry after that messenger, revise the former letter, and declare you will surely campaign together.
translations.idiomatic: Chase that rider, rewrite the letter, and swear you march as one.

sentences.zh: 若不及前信，宜更遣使。

translations.literal: If you cannot overtake the earlier courier, send another envoy.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot catch him, dispatch a fresh messenger.

sentences.zh: 」嶠意悟，即追信改書，侃果共征峻。

translations.literal: " Qiao grasped the point, immediately pursued the courier and altered the letter; Kan indeed joined the expedition against Jun.
translations.idiomatic: " Wen Qiao saw it, recalled the rider, revised the note, and Tao Kan agreed to strike Su Jun.

sentences.zh: 寶領千人為嶠前鋒，俱次茄子浦。

translations.literal: Bao led a thousand men as Qiao's vanguard; both halted at Eggplant Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao took a thousand men as Wen Qiao's van and camped at Eggplant Ford.

sentences.zh: 初，嶠以南軍習水，峻軍便步，欲以所長制之，宜令三軍，有上岸者死。

translations.literal: At first Qiao, because southern troops were practiced on water while Jun's army favored foot fighting, wished to leverage strength against weakness and ordered the three armies: whoever went ashore would die.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao bet on southern sailors against Su Jun's infantry and decreed death for anyone who landed.

sentences.zh: 時蘇峻送米萬斛饋祖約、約遣司馬桓撫等迎之。

translations.literal: At that time Su Jun sent ten thousand hu of grain as gift to Zu Yue; Yue dispatched Marshal Huan Fu and others to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun shipped ten thousand hu of grain to Zu Yue, who sent Huan Fu and staff to escort it.

sentences.zh: 寶告其眾曰：「兵法，軍令有所不從，豈可不上岸邪！

translations.literal: Bao told his men: "In the art of war, orders from headquarters may be disobeyed when circumstances demand—how can we refuse to go ashore!
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao harangued his troops: "War allows sensible disobedience—how can we stay dry?

sentences.zh: 」乃設變力戰，悉獲其米，虜殺萬計，約用大饑。

translations.literal: " He therefore improvised and fought fiercely, capturing all the grain, killing or capturing on the order of ten thousand, so Yue suffered great famine.
translations.idiomatic: " He improvised a landing, seized every sack, slaughtered thousands, and starved Zu Yue.

sentences.zh: 嶠嘉其勳，上為廬江太守。

translations.literal: Qiao praised his merit and memorialized him as Administrator of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao hailed the feat and memorialized him as administrator of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 約遣祖煥、桓撫等欲襲湓口，陶侃將自擊之，寶曰：「義軍恃公，公不可動，寶請討之。

translations.literal: Yue dispatched Zu Huan and Huan Fu and others intending to raid Yikou; Tao Kan meant to strike them personally; Bao said: "The righteous host looks to you—you cannot move; allow me to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue sent Zu Huan and Huan Fu toward Yikou; Tao Kan wanted to lead in person, but Mao Bao said: "The loyal army pins hope on you—stay; I will go.

sentences.zh: 」侃顧謂坐客曰：「此年少言可用也。

translations.literal: " Kan looked around at seated guests and said: "This young man's words can be used.
translations.idiomatic: " Tao Kan told his council: "The lad speaks sense.

sentences.zh: 」乃使寶行。

translations.literal: " He therefore sent Bao.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave Mao Bao the sortie.

sentences.zh: 先是，桓宣背約，南屯馬頭山，為煥、撫所攻，求救於寶。

translations.literal: Earlier Huan Xuan had broken with Yue and camped south at Mount Matou; Huan and Fu attacked him, and he begged rescue from Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Huan Xuan split from Zu Yue and held Mount Matou until Zu Huan and Huan Fu besieged him; he cried for Mao Bao.

sentences.zh: 寶眾以宣本是約黨，疑之。

translations.literal: Bao's troops considered Xuan originally Yue's partisan and doubted him.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao's men misliked Huan Xuan as one-time ally of Zu Yue.

sentences.zh: 宣遣子戎重請，寶即隨戎赴之。

translations.literal: Xuan sent his son Rong to plead urgently; Bao immediately followed Rong to him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan sent Huan Rong to insist; Mao Bao marched with him.

sentences.zh: 未至，而賊已與宣戰。

translations.literal: Before they arrived the bandits had already engaged Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: They arrived late—the enemy was already fighting Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 寶軍懸兵少，器杖濫惡，大為煥、撫所破。

translations.literal: Bao's army was isolated, few, and poorly armed; Huan and Fu shattered it.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao's handful bore rotten gear; Zu Huan and Huan Fu broke them.

sentences.zh: 寶中箭，貫髀徹鞍，使人蹋鞍拔箭，血流滿靴，夜奔船所百餘里，望星而行。

translations.literal: Bao took an arrow through thigh and saddle; he had a man stomp the saddle to draw the shaft; blood filled his boot; he fled by night more than a hundred li to the boats, steering by the stars.
translations.idiomatic: A bolt pinned Mao Bao's thigh through the saddle; a comrade stomped leather to free it while blood filled his boot; he ran a hundred li by starlight toward the fleet.

sentences.zh: 到，先哭戰亡將士，洗瘡訖，夜還救宣。

translations.literal: Arriving, he first wept for fallen officers, washed his wound, then by night returned to rescue Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He reached camp weeping for the dead, bathed the wound, then doubled back that night for Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 寶至宣營，而煥、撫亦退。

translations.literal: When Bao reached Xuan's camp, Huan and Fu had already withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Mao Bao joined Huan Xuan, Zu Huan and Huan Fu had slipped away.

sentences.zh: 寶進攻祖約，軍次東關，破合肥，尋召歸石頭。

translations.literal: Bao advanced against Zu Yue, halted at Dong Pass, took Hefei, and soon was summoned back to Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Zu Yue, camped at Dong Pass, seized Hefei, then was recalled to Stone Fort.

sentences.zh: 陶侃、溫嶠未能破賊，侃欲率眾南還。

translations.literal: Tao Kan and Wen Qiao could not yet break the bandits; Kan wished to lead the host southward.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan and Wen Qiao stalled; Kan talked of retreating south.

sentences.zh: 寶謂嶠曰：「下官能留之。

translations.literal: Bao told Qiao: "Your subordinate can keep him here.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao told Wen Qiao: "I can hold him.

sentences.zh: 」乃往說侃曰：「公本應領蕪湖，為南北勢援，前既已下，勢不可還。

translations.literal: " He went to persuade Kan: "You ought by rights to hold Wuhu as northern and southern hinge; having already come downstream, momentum forbids return.
translations.idiomatic: " He visited Tao Kan: "Wuhu should be your pivot between north and south; now that you have descended the river, withdrawal betrays momentum.

sentences.zh: 且軍政有進無退，非直整齊三軍，示眾必死而已，亦謂退無所據，終至滅亡。

translations.literal: Moreover military principle admits advance, not retreat—not merely to stiffen three armies and show certain death, but because retreat leaves nowhere to stand and ends in annihilation.
translations.idiomatic: War moves forward, never back—not only to steel the ranks but because retreat means nowhere to stand and certain ruin.

sentences.zh: 往者杜弢非不強盛，公竟滅之，何至於峻獨不可破邪！

translations.literal: Du Tao was not lacking in strength, yet you destroyed him—how can Jun alone be unbreakable!
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao was fierce—you crushed him—why fear Su Jun alone?

sentences.zh: 賊亦畏死，非皆勇健，公可試與寶兵，使上岸斷賊資糧，出其不意，使賊困蹙。

translations.literal: Bandits fear death too; not all are fearless heroes—try lending Bao troops to land, sever their supplies, catch them unprepared, and corner them.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels dread death no less—loan me men to cut their grain lines by surprise and choke them.

sentences.zh: 若寶不立效，然後公去，人心不恨。

translations.literal: If Bao achieves nothing, then my lord may withdraw without bitterness in men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: If I fail, withdraw then—no one will blame you.

sentences.zh: 」侃然之，加寶督護。

translations.literal: " Kan agreed and added Bao as protector.
translations.idiomatic: " Tao Kan assented and named Mao Bao protector.

sentences.zh: 寶燒峻句容、湖孰積聚，峻頗乏食，侃遂留不去。

translations.literal: Bao burned Jun's granaries at Jurong and Hushu; Jun grew short of food, so Kan stayed and did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao torched Su Jun's stockpiles at Jurong and Hushu; hunger pinned Su Jun so Tao Kan remained.

sentences.zh: 峻既死，匡術以苑城降。

translations.literal: After Jun died, Kuang Shu surrendered the imperial park city.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun's fall brought Kuang Shu's surrender of the park citadel.

sentences.zh: 侃使寶守南城，鄧嶽守西城。

translations.literal: Kan ordered Bao to hold the south wall and Deng Yue the west.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan set Mao Bao on the south rampart and Deng Yue on the west.

sentences.zh: 賊遣韓晃攻之，寶登城射殺數十人。

translations.literal: The bandits sent Han Huang to attack them; Bao mounted the wall and shot dozens dead.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang stormed the gate; Mao Bao rained bolts and dropped dozens.

sentences.zh: 晃問寶曰：「君是毛廬江邪？

translations.literal: Huang asked Bao: "Are you Mao of Lujiang?
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang called: "Are you Mao the Lujiang man?

sentences.zh: 」寶曰：「是。

translations.literal: " Bao said: "Yes.
translations.idiomatic: " Mao Bao answered: "I am.

sentences.zh: 」晃曰：「君名壯勇，何不出鬥！

translations.literal: " Huang said: "Your name speaks of valor—why not come out and duel!
translations.idiomatic: " "They say you are fierce—step out and fight!

sentences.zh: 」寶曰：「君若健將，何不入鬥！

translations.literal: " Bao said: "If you are a stalwart general, why not enter the fight!
translations.idiomatic: " "If you are a real champion, climb the wall yourself!

sentences.zh: 」晃笑而退。

translations.literal: " Huang laughed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Han Huang laughed and backed off.

sentences.zh: 賊平，封州陵縣開國侯，千六百戶。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was enfeoffed Founding Marquis of Zhouling County with sixteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Peace won him founding marquis of Zhouling with sixteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 庾亮西鎮，請為輔國將軍、江夏相、督隨義陽二郡，鎮上明。

translations.literal: When Yu Liang moved west to command, he requested Bao as general Who Supports the State, Chancellor of Jiangxia, supervising Suí and Yiyang commanderies, garrisoning Shangming.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang's western command took Mao Bao as general Who Supports the State, chancellor of Jiangxia, overseeing Suí and Yiyang, posted at Shangming.

sentences.zh: 又進南中郎。

translations.literal: He was further promoted General of the Southern Palace Court.
translations.idiomatic: He rose again to general of the southern palace court.

sentences.zh: 隨亮討郭默。

translations.literal: He followed Liang against Guo Mo.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Yu Liang against Guo Mo.

sentences.zh: 默平，與亮司馬王愆期救桓宣于章山，擊賊將石遇，破之，進征虜將軍。

translations.literal: After Mo was crushed, together with Liang's aide Wang Yanqi he rescued Huan Xuan at Zhang Mountain, struck bandit commander Shi Yu, defeated him, and was promoted general Who Conquers the Caitiffs.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guo Mo fell he joined Wang Yanqi to relieve Huan Xuan on Zhang Mountain, broke Shi Yu, and earned the generalship Who Conquers the Caitiffs.

sentences.zh: 亮謀北伐，上疏解豫州，請以授寶。

translations.literal: Liang planned a northern expedition and memorialized to yield Yuzhou, asking it be granted to Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang aimed north and offered Yuzhou to Mao Bao.

sentences.zh: 於是詔以寶監揚州之江西諸軍事、豫州刺史，將軍如故，與西陽太守樊峻以萬人守邾城。

translations.literal: An edict therefore ordered Bao to supervise all military affairs west of the river in Yangzhou with concurrent appointment as Inspector of Yuzhou, general as before, together with Administrator of Xiyang Fan Jun holding Zhucheng with ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The throne named Mao Bao overseer of Jiangxi military affairs and inspector of Yuzhou at his old rank, pairing him with Fan Jun of Xiyang and ten thousand men at Zhucheng.

sentences.zh: 石季龍惡之，乃遣其子鑒與其將夔安、李菟等五萬人來寇，張狢渡二萬騎攻邾城。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong hated this and sent his son Jian with commanders Kui An, Li Tu, and others—fifty thousand men—to invade; Zhang Huo led twenty thousand horse across the ford against Zhucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jilong answered with fifty thousand men under Shi Jian, Kui An, and Li Tu; Zhang Huo splashed twenty thousand cavalry toward Zhucheng.

sentences.zh: 寶求救於亮，亮以城固，不時遣軍，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Bao begged rescue from Liang; Liang, trusting the walls, did not dispatch troops in time, so the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao cried for help; Yu Liang trusted the masonry and tarried until Zhucheng collapsed.

sentences.zh: 寶、峻等率左右突圍出，赴江死者六千人，寶亦溺死。

translations.literal: Bao, Jun, and others broke out with their guard; six thousand died rushing into the river; Bao also drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao, Fan Jun, and escort hacked free; six thousand drowned in the Yangzi—Mao Bao sank with them.

sentences.zh: 亮哭之慟，因發疾，遂薨。

translations.literal: Liang wept bitterly, fell ill on account of it, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang mourned until grief broke his health and killed him.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「寶之傾敗，宜在貶裁。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Bao's collapse merits demotion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Mao Bao's rout calls for censure.

sentences.zh: 然蘇峻之難，致力王室。

translations.literal: Yet during Su Jun's crisis he exerted himself for the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Su Jun's war he spent himself for the throne.

sentences.zh: 今咎其過，故不加贈，祭之可也。

translations.literal: Now, blaming his fault, we add no posthumous honors; sacrifice to him may proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Blame his lapse—grant no posthumous rank—but allow offerings.

sentences.zh: 」其後公卿言寶有重勳，加死王事，不宜奪爵。

translations.literal: " Later ministers argued Bao had heavy merit, died on duty, and ought not lose his nobility.
translations.idiomatic: " Ministers later insisted Mao Bao's service outweighed the defeat—stripping his title wronged a martyr.

sentences.zh: 升平三年，乃下詔復本封。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengping an edict restored his original enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengping year three the throne restored his original fief.

sentences.zh: 初，寶在武昌，軍人有于市買得一白龜，長四五寸，養之漸大，放諸江中。

translations.literal: At first, while Bao was at Wuchang, a soldier bought a white turtle four or five inches long in the market, raised it until it grew large, and released it into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Wuchang a soldier bought a palm-sized white turtle, raised it to adulthood, and freed it in the Long River.

sentences.zh: 邾城之敗，養龜人被鎧持刀，自投于水中，如覺墮一石上，視之，乃先所養白龜，長五六尺，送至東岸，遂得免焉。

translations.literal: At the fall of Zhucheng the turtle-keeper donned armor, seized a blade, and threw himself into the water; it felt like landing on a stone—looking, it was the former white turtle, five or six chi long, which carried him to the eastern bank so he survived.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhucheng fell that same man leaped armored into the flood and struck what felt like rock—the giant white turtle he had freed, now six feet long, ferried him east and saved his life.

sentences.zh: 寶二子：穆之、安之。

translations.literal: Bao had two sons: Muzhi and Anzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao fathered Muzhi and Anzhi.

sentences.zh: 穆之字憲祖，小字武生，名犯王靖後諱，故行字，後又以桓溫母名憲，乃更稱小字。

translations.literal: Muzhi styled Xianzu, childhood name Wusheng; his given name violated the later taboo on Wang Jing, so he used his courtesy name; later because Huan Wen's mother was named Xian he reverted to the childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi took courtesy Xianzu and childhood name Wusheng; taboo on Wang Jing blocked the formal name, so he lived by his courtesy until Huan Wen's mother named Xian forced him back to the childhood name.

sentences.zh: 穆之果毅有父風，安西將軍庾翼以為參軍。

translations.literal: Muzhi was resolute like his father; general Who Pacifies the West Yu Yi took him as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi matched his father's grit; Yu Yi, general Who Pacifies the West, enlisted him.

sentences.zh: 襲爵州陵侯，翼等專威陝西，以子方之為建武將軍，守襄陽。

translations.literal: He inherited the marquisate of Zhouling; Yi and colleagues wielded power west of the passes and appointed son Fangzhi general Who Displays Martial Might to guard Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to Zhouling marquis as Yu Yi dominated Shaanxi and posted son Yu Fangzhi as general Who Displays Might at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 方之年少，翼選武將可信杖者為輔弼，乃以穆之為建武司馬。

translations.literal: Fangzhi was young; Yi chose reliable warriors to assist him and named Muzhi major clerk under the general Who Displays Might.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fangzhi's youth moved Yu Yi to pick trustworthy fighters as props and make Muzhi military clerk under the general Who Displays Might.

sentences.zh: 俄而翼薨，大將幹瓚、戴羲等作亂，穆之與安西長史江虨、司馬硃燾等共平之。

translations.literal: Soon Yi died; senior generals Gan Zan and Dai Xi rebelled; Muzhi together with chief clerk Jiang Bin and marshal Zhu Tao pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi's death sparked mutiny from Gan Zan and Dai Xi; Muzhi, chief clerk Jiang Bin, and marshal Zhu Tao crushed it.

sentences.zh: 桓溫代翼，復取為參軍。

translations.literal: Huan Wen succeeded Yi and again took him as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen replaced Yu Yi and pulled Mao Muzhi back onto staff.

sentences.zh: 從溫平蜀，以功賜次子都鄉侯。

translations.literal: He followed Wen to pacify Shu and for merit his second son was granted Village Marquis of Duxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Huan Wen against Shu and won the lesser heir the village marquisate of Duxiang.

sentences.zh: 尋除揚威將軍、潁川太守，隨溫平洛，入關。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed to general Who Displays Martial Glory and Administrator of Yingchuan; he followed Wen to pacify Luoyang and entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion followed to general Who Displays Glory and Yingchuan administrator; he entered Guanzhong on Huan Wen's Luoyang campaign.

sentences.zh: 溫將旋師，以謝尚未至，留穆之以二千人衛山陵。

translations.literal: When Wen prepared to wheel the army homeward because Xie had not yet arrived, he left Muzhi with two thousand men to guard the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen meant to withdraw before Xie's column arrived, so he detached Mao Muzhi with two thousand soldiers to watch the mausolea.

sentences.zh: 升平初，遷督甯州諸軍事、揚威將軍、甯州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shengping era he was transferred to supervise all military affairs of Ningzhou, general Who Displays Martial Glory, and Inspector of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early Shengping brought command over Ningzhou armies, the glory generalship, and the Ningzhou inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 以桓溫封南郡，徙穆之為建安侯，復為溫太尉參軍。

translations.literal: Because Huan Wen was enfeoffed Prince of Nan Commandery, Muzhi was shifted to Marquis of Jian'an and again became aide to Wen as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's Nan principality shifted Mao Muzhi's fief to Jian'an marquis and returned him to the Grand Commandant's office.

sentences.zh: 加冠軍將軍，以所募兵配之。

translations.literal: He was additionally named Champion general and the troops he had recruited were assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: They added champion general and handed him the recruits he had raised.

sentences.zh: 溫伐慕容暐，使穆之監鑿钜野百餘里，引汶會於濟川。

translations.literal: When Wen campaigned against Murong Wei, he had Muzhi supervise cutting a channel more than a hundred li through Juye to draw the Wen River into the Ji River.
translations.idiomatic: Against Former Yan he tasked Mao Muzhi with dredging Juye—over a hundred li—to merge the Wen into the Ji.

sentences.zh: 及溫焚舟步歸，使穆之督東燕四郡軍事。

translations.literal: When Wen burned his boats and marched home on foot, he made Muzhi supervise military affairs of four Dongyan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Wen torched his fleet and walked home, Mao Muzhi governed four Dongyan counties.

sentences.zh: 領東燕太守，本官如故。

translations.literal: He held concurrent appointment as Administrator of Dongyan with original offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed Dongyan administrator while keeping former titles.

sentences.zh: 袁真以壽陽叛，溫將征之。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhen rebelled at Shouyang; Wen prepared to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen turned traitor at Shouyang and Huan Wen readied an expedition.

sentences.zh: 穆之以冠軍領淮南太守，守曆陽。

translations.literal: Muzhi as Champion general held concurrent Administrator of Huainan and guarded Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Muzhi held champion rank, Huainan magistracy, and the Liyang line.

sentences.zh: 真平，餘黨分散，乃以穆之督揚州之江西軍事，復領陳郡太守。

translations.literal: After Zhen was crushed and remnants scattered, Muzhi was assigned to supervise Jiangxi military affairs in Yangzhou and again held Administrator of Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen's fall scattered diehards; Mao Muzhi took Yangzhou's river-west armies plus Chen commandery again.

sentences.zh: 俄而徙督揚州之義成荊州五郡雍州之兆軍事、襄陽義成河南三郡太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was shifted to supervise military affairs of Yicheng in Yangzhou, five commanderies in Jingzhou, and Fengyi in Yongzhou, where the received graph zhao in the source is emended in most editions to Fengyi, with concurrent appointment as Administrator of Xiangyang, Yicheng, and Henan, general as before.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to command Yicheng plus five Jingzhou counties and Yongzhou's Fengyi circuit—still general while administering Xiangyang, Yicheng, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 尋進領梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he advanced to concurrent Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after he added the Liangzhou inspector's seal.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以疾解職，詔以冠軍征還。

translations.literal: Before long he resigned on grounds of illness; an edict summoned him back as Champion general.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced retirement until the court recalled him under champion rank.

sentences.zh: 苻堅別將寇彭城，復以將軍假節、監江北軍事。

translations.literal: When a detached commander of Fu Jian raided Pengcheng, he was again named general with credential staff and supervisor of military affairs north of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's lieutenant struck Pengcheng; Mao Muzhi returned as credential general overseeing the north bank.

sentences.zh: 鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: He garrisoned Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He held Guangling.

sentences.zh: 遷右將軍、宣城內史、假節，鎮姑孰。

translations.literal: He was promoted general of the Right, Interior Secretary of Xuancheng with credential staff, garrisoning Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion brought general of the right, Xuancheng interior secretary, credential staff, and a post at Gushu.

sentences.zh: 穆之以為戍在近畿，無復軍警，不宜加節，上疏辭讓，許之。

translations.literal: Muzhi considered that the garrison lay near the capital precincts where military alarms no longer arose; it was inappropriate to add credential staff—he memorialized to decline, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that guarding the inner zone meant no banner was needed; the throne accepted his refusal of the staff.

sentences.zh: 苻堅別將圍襄陽，詔穆之就上明受桓沖節度。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian's detached commander besieged Xiangyang, an edict ordered Muzhi to receive orders from Huan Chong at Shangming.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's siege drew an order for Mao Muzhi to fall under Huan Chong at Shangming.

sentences.zh: 沖使穆之遊軍沔中。

translations.literal: Chong ordered Muzhi to roam the army along the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong told him to patrol the Han basin.

sentences.zh: 穆之始至，而硃序陷沒，引軍還郡。

translations.literal: Hardly had Muzhi arrived when Zhu Xu fell captive; he led the army back to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu's capture broke the relief before it landed; Mao Muzhi withdrew to his seat.

sentences.zh: 堅眾又寇蜀漢，梁州刺史楊亮、益州刺史周仲孫奔退，沖使穆之督梁州之三郡軍事、右將軍、西蠻校尉、益州刺史、領建平太守、假節，戍巴郡。

translations.literal: Jian's host next raided Shu and Han; Inspector of Liangzhou Yang Liang and Inspector of Yizhou Zhou Zhongsun fled in retreat; Chong ordered Muzhi to supervise military affairs of three Liangzhou commanderies with concurrent appointments as general of the Right, Colonel Who Subdues the Western Yi, Inspector of Yizhou, Administrator of Jianping with credential staff, garrisoning Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's next thrust hit Shu-Han; Yang Liang and Zhou Zhongsun bolted; Huan Chong piled on Mao Muzhi—three Liangzhou sectors, general of the right, western Yi colonel, Yizhou inspector, Jianping administrator, credential staff, holding Ba.

sentences.zh: 以子球為梓潼太守。

translations.literal: He appointed his son Qiu Administrator of Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: He named son Mao Qiu magistrate of Zitong.

sentences.zh: 穆之與球伐堅，至於巴西郡，以糧運乏少，退屯巴東，病卒。

translations.literal: Muzhi and Qiu campaigned against Jian as far as Ba-Xi Commandery; grain ran short, so they withdrew to camp at Badong; Muzhi died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son reached Ba-Xi but starvation drove them back to Badong, where Mao Muzhi died.

sentences.zh: 追贈中軍將軍，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as general of the Central Army; posthumous title Martyr.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous rank hit central army general with the martyr epithet.

sentences.zh: 子珍嗣，位至天門太守。

translations.literal: His son Zhen inherited and rose to Administrator of Tianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Mao Zhen climbed to Tianmen administrator.

sentences.zh: 珍弟璩、球、璠、瑾、瑗，璩最知名。

translations.literal: Younger brothers of Zhen were Qu, Qiu, Fan, Jin, and Yuan; Qu was best known.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's brothers Qu, Qiu, Fan, Jin, and Yuan followed—Qu stood tallest in fame.

sentences.zh: 璩字叔璉。

translations.literal: Qu styled Shulian.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Qu took courtesy Shulian.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，右將軍桓豁以為參軍。

translations.literal: At weak-cap age general of the Right Huan He took him as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Coming of age he entered Huan He's service as aide.

sentences.zh: 尋遭父憂，服闕，為謝安衛將軍參軍，除尚書郎。

translations.literal: Soon he suffered his father's mourning; when mourning ended he became aide to Xie An's Guard general and was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral leave followed his father's death; then Xie An's guard office and secretariat appointment.

sentences.zh: 安復請為參軍，轉安子琰征虜司馬。

translations.literal: An again requested him as aide and transferred him to be expedition marshal under An's son Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An pulled him back as aide and shifted him to expedition marshal under Xie Yan.

sentences.zh: 淮肥之役，苻堅迸走，璩與田次之共躡堅，至中陽，不及而歸。

translations.literal: At the Huai-Fei campaign, when Fu Jian broke and fled, Qu together with Tian Cizi pursued Jian to Zhongyang but did not catch him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian ran from Fei River, Mao Qu and Tian Cizi chased him to Zhongyang without closing the kill.

sentences.zh: 遷甯朔將軍、淮南太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted general Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to northern pacifier and Huainan magistrate.

sentences.zh: 尋補鎮北將軍、譙王恬司馬。

translations.literal: Soon he filled the post of marshal to Prince of Qiao Wang Tian, general Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: Next he served Prince Wang Tian of Qiao as marshal under the northern guard general.

sentences.zh: 海陵縣界地名青蒲，四面湖澤，皆是菰葑，逃亡所聚，威令不能及。

translations.literal: Within Hailing County lay a place called Green Reed surrounded on four sides by lakes and marshes—all arrowroot and reed mats—where fugitives gathered beyond the reach of awe and decree.
translations.idiomatic: Green Reed in Hailing was ringed by lakes choked with mat-grass where outlaws hid beyond the law.

sentences.zh: 璩建議率千討人。

translations.literal: Qu proposed leading a thousand men to strike them (received text appears abbreviated).
translations.idiomatic: Mao Qu asked for a thousand blades to scour the swamp—scribes likely dropped words after thousand.

sentences.zh: 時大旱，璩因放火，菰葑盡然，亡戶窘迫，悉出詣璩自首，近有萬戶，皆以補兵，朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: At that time severe drought enabled Qu to set fires that burned the mats clear; refugee households, desperate, all presented themselves to Qu to surrender—nearly ten thousand households were drafted as soldiers, and the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Drought let him burn the reed flats bare; tens of thousands crept out to enlist and the court cheered.

sentences.zh: 轉西中郎司馬、龍驤將軍、譙梁二郡內史。

translations.literal: He was transferred Western Palace marshal, general Soaring Dragon, and Interior Secretary of Qiao and Liang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Moves stacked up: western palace marshal, Soaring Dragon general, interior secretary over Qiao and Liang.

sentences.zh: 尋代郭銓為建威將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Guo Quan as general Who Displays Martial Might and Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded Guo Quan as mighty-display general and Yizhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 安帝初，進征虜將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor An's reign he was promoted general Who Conquers the Caitiffs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An's opening years brought the caitiff-conquering generalship.

sentences.zh: 及桓玄篡位，遣使加璩散騎常侍、左將軍。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne he sent envoys to add Qu ordinary attendant cavalier and general of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan's coup brought messengers offering Mao Qu left general and ordinary attendant.

sentences.zh: 璩執留玄使，不受命。

translations.literal: Qu detained Xuan's envoy and refused the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Qu locked up the envoy and rejected the patent.

sentences.zh: 玄以桓希為梁州刺史，王異據涪，郭法戍宕渠，師寂戍巴郡，周道子戍白帝以防之。

translations.literal: Xuan appointed Huan Xi Inspector of Liangzhou; Wang Yi held Fu; Guo Fa held Dangqu; Shi Ji held Ba Commandery; Zhou Daozi held Baidicheng to block him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan ringed him with Huan Xi in Liangzhou, Wang Yi on the Fu, Guo Fa at Dangqu, Shi Ji in Ba, Zhou Daozi at White Emperor.

sentences.zh: 璩傳檄遠近，列玄罪狀，遣巴東太守柳約之、建平太守羅述、征虜司馬甄季之擊破希等，仍率眾次於白帝。

translations.literal: Qu circulated proclamations far and near listing Xuan's crimes; he dispatched Administrator of Badong Liu Yuezhi, Administrator of Jianping Luo Shu, and expedition marshal Zhen Jizhi to crush Xi and others, then led troops to halt at Baidicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Manifestos flew; Liu Yuezhi, Luo Shu, and Zhen Jizhi smashed Huan Xi while Mao Qu anchored at Baidicheng.

sentences.zh: 武陵王令曰：「益州刺史毛璩忠誠愨亮，自桓玄萌禍，常思躡其後。

translations.literal: Prince of Wuling's order said: "Inspector of Yizhou Mao Qu is loyal, sincere, and bright; since Huan Xuan bred calamity he has long plotted to tread on Xuan's heels.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wuling wrote: "Yizhou inspector Mao Qu proved steadfast—he aimed at Huan Xuan's back from the first.

sentences.zh: 今若平殄凶逆，肅清荊郢者，便當即授上流之任。」

translations.literal: If now he levels the traitors and clears Jing and Ying, he shall immediately receive appointment to the upper Yangzi command."
translations.idiomatic: Crush the usurper and cleanse Jing-Ying, and the upper river command is his."

sentences.zh: 初，璩弟甯州刺史璠卒官，璩兄球孫祐之及參軍費恬以數百人送喪，葬江陵。

translations.literal: At first Qu's younger brother Fan, Inspector of Ningzhou, died in office; Qu's elder brother Qiu's grandson Youzhi together with aide Fei Tian escorted the funeral with several hundred men and buried him at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao Fan fell as Ningzhou inspector, grandson Youzhi and Fei Tian convoyed the bier with hundreds to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 會玄敗，謀奔梁州。

translations.literal: It happened that Xuan had been defeated and they plotted to flee toward Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan's rout sent them scheming toward Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 璩弟瑾子修之時為玄屯騎校尉，誘玄使入蜀，既而修之與祐之、費恬及漢嘉人馮遷共殺玄。

translations.literal: Qu's younger brother Jin's son Xiuzhi was then Xuan's cavalry colonel; he lured Xuan into Shu, after which Xiuzhi together with Youzhi, Fei Tian, and Feng Qian of Hanjia jointly killed Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jin's son Xiuzhi, Xuan's cavalry colonel, baited him into Shu, then with Youzhi, Fei Tian, and Feng Qian cut him down.

sentences.zh: 約之等聞玄死，進軍到枝復攻沒江陵。

translations.literal: When Yuezhi and company heard Xuan was dead, they advanced to Zhijiang, again attacked, and took Jiangling (received punctuation splits the phrase).
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuezhi marched to Zhijiang, struck again, and seized Jiangling on news of Xuan's death.

sentences.zh: 劉毅等還尋陽，約之亦退。

translations.literal: When Liu Yi and others returned to Xunyang, Yuezhi also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi's retreat to Xunyang pulled Yuezhi back too.

sentences.zh: 俄而季子、述皆病，約子詣振偽降，因欲襲振而桓振。

translations.literal: Before long Jizhi and Shu both fell ill; Yuezhi's son went to Huan Zhen feigning surrender, intending to strike Zhen—and Huan Zhen saw through it (received text breaks mid-clause; 而桓振 likely garbled).
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhen Jizhi and Luo Shu sickened; Liu Yuezhi's son faked defection to ambush Huan Zhen—who caught the plot.

sentences.zh: 事泄，被害。

translations.literal: The affair leaked and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Word slipped out and he died for it.

sentences.zh: 約之司馬時延祖、涪陵太守文處茂等撫其餘眾，保涪陵。

translations.literal: Yuezhi's marshal Shi Yanzu and Administrator of Fuling Wen Chumao then soothed the surviving host and held Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Shi Yanzu and Wen Chumao of Fuling rallied the remnant behind Fuling's walls.

sentences.zh: 振遣桓放之為益州，屯西陵。

translations.literal: Zhen dispatched Huan Fangzhi as Inspector of Yizhou and camped at Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Zhen sent Huan Fangzhi toward Yizhou and camped west of the rapids.

sentences.zh: 處茂距擊，破之。

translations.literal: Chumao resisted and struck him, defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Chumao met him head-on and broke his force.

sentences.zh: 振死，安帝反正，詔曰：「夫貞松標於歲寒，忠臣亮于國危。

translations.literal: When Zhen died and Emperor An regained the throne, an edict said: "The steadfast pine stands out in bitter cold; the loyal minister shines when the state is in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Zhen's death freed Emperor An; an edict mused: winter reveals the hardy pine—crisis reveals loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史璩體識弘正，誠契義旗，受命偏師，次於近畿，匡翼之勳，實感朕心。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yizhou Qu grasped the great pattern and kept faith with the righteous banner; receiving command of a detached division he halted near the capital precincts—the merit of aiding and sheltering truly moves Us.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Qu read the larger loyalty, backed the restoration army, and camped at the capital's elbow—his shelter of the throne touched us.

sentences.zh: 可進征西將軍，加散騎常侍，都督益梁秦涼寧五州軍事，行宜都、甯蜀太守。

translations.literal: He may be promoted general Who Conquers the West with additional ordinary attendant cavalier and supervisor of military affairs over Yi, Liang (principal commandery), Qin, Liang (northern frontier), and Ning—five provinces—acting Administrator of Yidu and Ningshu.
translations.idiomatic: Promote him west-conquering general, ordinary attendant, governor of Yi, Liang on the Han, Qin, Hexi Liang, and Ning, acting Yidu and Ningshu magistrate.

sentences.zh: 文處茂宣贊蕃牧，蒙險夷難，可輔國將軍、西夷校尉、巴西梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: Wen Chumao who proclaimed order in the outer marches and braved passes and hardship may become general Who Supports the State, Colonel of the Western Yi, and Administrator of Ba and Zitong commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Chumao, who held the frontier through peril, earns supporting-state general, western Yi colonel, and twin magistracies in Ba and Zitong.

sentences.zh: 」又詔西夷校尉瑾為持節、監梁秦二州軍事、征虜將軍、梁秦二州刺史、略陽武都太守。

translations.literal: " Another edict named Mao Jin, Colonel of the Western Yi, as credential bearer supervising Liang and Qin military affairs, general Who Conquers the Caitiffs, Inspector of Liang and Qin, Administrator of Lüeyang and Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: " Mao Jin kept western Yi colonel but gained credential staff over Liang-Qin, caitiff general, twin inspector, Lüeyang-Wudu administrator.

sentences.zh: 瑾弟蜀郡太守瑗為輔國將軍、甯州刺史。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother Yuan, Administrator of Shu Commandery, became general Who Supports the State and Inspector of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Younger Mao Yuan kept Shu magistracy while gaining supporting general and Ningzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 初，璩聞振陷江陵，率眾赴難，使瑾、瑗順外江而下，使參軍譙縱領巴西、梓潼二郡軍下涪水，當與璩軍會于巴郡。

translations.literal: At first, when Qu heard Zhen had taken Jiangling, he led troops to the rescue; he ordered Jin and Yuan down the outer Yangzi while aide Qiao Zong led Ba and Zitong troops down the Fu River to join Qu at Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Jiangling had fallen, Mao Qu marched relief: Jin and Yuan on the main stream, Qiao Zong on the Fu, rendezvousing at Ba.

sentences.zh: 蜀人不樂東征，縱因人情思歸，于五城水口反，還襲涪，害瑾，瑾留府長史鄭純之自成都馳使告璩。

translations.literal: The people of Shu had no wish to march east; Zong exploited their longing for home and rebelled at Wucheng Ford, doubled back to strike Fu, killed Jin, while Jin's chief clerk Zheng Chunzhi galloped from Chengdu to warn Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu men refused an eastern war; Qiao Zong mutinied at Wucheng, wheeled on Fu, slew Mao Jin, while Zheng Chunzhi raced word to Mao Qu.

sentences.zh: 璩時在略城，去成都四百里，遣參軍王瓊討反者，相距於廣漢。

translations.literal: Qu was then at Lucheng, four hundred li from Chengdu; he dispatched aide Wang Qiong to punish the rebels; they faced each other at Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Qu held Lucheng, four hundred li from Chengdu, and sent Wang Qiong to duel Qiao Zong at Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 僰道令何林聚黨助縱，而璩下人受縱誘說，遂共害璩及瑗，並子侄之在蜀者，一時殄沒。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Bodao He Lin gathered a band to aid Zong, while Qu's own men succumbed to Zong's blandishments and together murdered Qu and Yuan along with sons and nephews then in Shu—all perished at once.
translations.idiomatic: He Lin of Bodao backed Qiao Zong; Mao Qu's soldiers flipped, slaughtering Mao Qu, Mao Yuan, and every kinsman in Shu.

sentences.zh: 璩子弘之嗣。

translations.literal: Qu's son Hongzhi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Mao Hongzhi inherited.

sentences.zh: 義熙中，時延祖為始康太守，上疏訟璩兄弟，於是詔曰：「故益州刺史璩、西夷校尉瑾、蜀郡太守瑗勤王忠烈，事乖慮外。

translations.literal: During the Yixi era Shi Yanzu, Administrator of Shikang, memorialized to plead the case of Qu's brothers; an edict therefore said: "The late Inspector of Yizhou Qu, Colonel of the Western Yi Jin, and Administrator of Shu Commandery Yuan served the king with fierce loyalty yet met fate beyond planning.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi years brought Shi Yanzu's plea for the Mao brothers; the throne answered: they died loyal though heaven cheated them.

sentences.zh: 葬送日近，益懷惻愴，可皆贈先所授官，給錢三十萬、布三百匹。

translations.literal: Their burial draws near and Our grief deepens; restore each to his former rank, grant three hundred thousand cash and three hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: As burial nears our ache grows—restore former offices, grant three hundred thousand cash and three hundred bolts.

sentences.zh: 」論璩討桓玄功，追封歸鄉公，千五百戶。

translations.literal: " Judging Qu's merit in attacking Huan Xuan, posthumous enfeoffment as Duke of Guixiang with fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For crushing Huan Xuan Mao Qu won posthumous Duke of Guixiang at fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又以祐之斬玄功，封夷道縣侯。

translations.literal: Also for Youzhi's merit in beheading Xuan, enfeoff him Marquis of Yidao County.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi's blade on Xuan earned the Yidao county marquisate.

sentences.zh: 自寶至璩三葉，擁旄開國者四人，將帥之家，與尋陽周氏為輩，而人物不及也。

translations.literal: From Bao down to Qu spanned three generations; four men bore credential staffs and founding marquisates—a house of generals ranked with the Zhou clan of Xunyang though its talents fell short.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations from Mao Bao to Mao Qu produced four banner-bearing founders—peer to Xunyang's Zhous if lesser in brilliance.

sentences.zh: 瑾子修之，頻曆清顯，至右衛將軍，從劉裕平姚泓。

translations.literal: Jin's son Xiuzhi repeatedly rose through pure appointments to general of the Right Guards and followed Liu Yu in pacifying Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi climbed clean posts to right guards general and joined Liu Yu against Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 後為安西司馬，沒于魏。

translations.literal: Later he became marshal of the Guard general of the West and was lost to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Later western guard marshal, he vanished into Wei captivity.

sentences.zh: 四子：潭、泰、邃、遁。

translations.literal: Four sons: Tan, Tai, Sui, and Dun.
translations.idiomatic: He fathered Tan, Tai, Sui, and Dun.

sentences.zh: 潭嗣爵，官至江夏相。

translations.literal: Tan inherited the nobility and rose to Chancellor of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest Mao Tan took the title and reached Jiangxia chancellor.

sentences.zh: 泰曆太傅從事中郎、後軍諮議參軍，與邃俱為會稽王父子所昵，乃追論安之討盧悚勳，賜爵平都子，命潭襲爵。

translations.literal: Tai served successively as attendant clerk to the Grand Tutor and advisory aide to the Rear Army; both he and Sui were intimate favorites of Prince of Kuaiji and his son; the court retroactively judged Anzhi's merit against Lu Song and granted Tai the noble rank Baron of Pingdu, ordering Tan to inherit the main marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Tai advised the Grand Tutor and rear army; he and Mao Sui curried Prince Kuaiji's circle until Lu Song's old score won Tai the Pingdu barony while Tan kept the main line.

sentences.zh: 元顯嘗宴泰家，既而欲去，泰苦留之曰：「公若遂去，當取公腳。

translations.literal: Yuan Xian once feasted at Tai's home and afterward wished to leave; Tai urgently detained him saying: "If my lord insists on going I shall take your legs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian dined at Mao Tai's then rose to leave; Mao Tai joked he would take his legs if he walked out.

sentences.zh: 」元顯大怒，奮衣而出，遂與元顯有隙。

translations.literal: Yuan Xian was furious, shook his robes and departed, and thereafter bore ill will toward Tai.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Xian stormed out—and enmity opened between him and Mao Tai.

sentences.zh: 及元顯敗，泰時為冠軍將軍、堂邑太山二郡太守。

translations.literal: When Yuan Xian fell, Tai was then Champion general and concurrent Administrator of Tangyi and Taishan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuan Xian's ruin Mao Tai held champion rank over Tangyi and Taishan.

sentences.zh: 邃為遊擊將軍，遁為太傅主簿，桓玄得志，使泰收元顯，遂於新亭，泰因宿恨，手加毆辱。

translations.literal: Sui was Roaming Strike general; Dun was chief clerk to the Grand Tutor; when Huan Xuan achieved his ambition he ordered Tai to seize Yuan Xian; Tai caught him at Xin Pavilion and, nursing old hatred, personally struck and humiliated him.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Sui served as roaming striker; Mao Dun clerked the Grand Tutor; Huan Xuan ordered Mao Tai to collar Yuan Xian at Xin Pavilion—where Mao Tai repaid old insults with his fists.

sentences.zh: 俄並為玄所殺，惟遁被徙廣州。

translations.literal: Soon both were killed by Xuan; only Dun was banished to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan soon executed both brothers; only Mao Dun went south in exile.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，得還，至宜都太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi he was allowed to return and reached Administrator of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi's opening saw him home as Yidu magistrate.

sentences.zh: 德祖，璩宗人也。

translations.literal: Dezu was a clansman of Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Dezu belonged to Mao Qu's lineage.

sentences.zh: 父祖並沒於賊中。

translations.literal: Father and grandfather both perished amid bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Father and grandfather died in rebel chaos.

sentences.zh: 德祖兄弟五人，相攜南渡，皆有武幹，荊州刺史劉道規以德祖為建武將軍、始平太守，又徙涪陵太守。

translations.literal: Dezu had five brothers who crossed south together; all possessed martial talent; Inspector of Jingzhou Liu Daogui appointed Dezu general Who Displays Martial Might and Administrator of Shiping, later transferring him to Administrator of Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: Five Mao brothers fled south together; Liu Daogui made Mao Dezu mighty-display general, Shiping magistrate, then Fuling.

sentences.zh: 盧循之役，道規又以為參軍，伐徐道覆於始興。

translations.literal: During Lu Xun's campaign Daogui again employed him as aide and sent him against Xu Daofu at Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun's war brought Mao Dezu back as aide against Xu Daofu at Shixing.

sentences.zh: 尋遭母憂。

translations.literal: Soon he suffered his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Mother's death soon pulled him into mourning.

sentences.zh: 劉裕伐司馬休之，版補太尉參軍、義陽太守，賜爵遷陵縣侯，轉南陽太守，從劉裕伐姚泓，頻攻滎陽、扶風、南安、馮詡數郡，所在克捷。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu campaigned against Sima Xiuzhi, he was appointed by emergency patent Grand Commandant aide and Administrator of Yiyang with noble rank Marquis of Qianling County; he was transferred Administrator of Nanyang and followed Liu Yu against Yao Hong, repeatedly attacking Xingyang, Fufeng, Nan'an, and Fengyi commanderies—everywhere victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's march on Sima Xiuzhi drafted Mao Dezu as Grand Commandant aide and Yiyang magistrate with Qianling marquisate; Nanyang followed, then conquest of Later Qin—Xingyang, Fufeng, Nan'an, Fengyi fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 裕嘉之，以為龍驤將軍、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Yu praised him and named him general Soaring Dragon and Inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu rewarded him with Soaring Dragon general and Qinzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 裕留第二子義真為安西將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Yu left his second son Yizhen as general Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu left Liu Yizhen as western pacifier and Yongzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 以德祖為中兵參軍，領天水太守，從義真還。

translations.literal: He appointed Dezu central corps aide with concurrent Administrator of Tianshui, following Yizhen home.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Dezu served as central corps aide and Tianshui magistrate on the withdrawal with Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 裕以德祖督河東平陽二郡軍事、輔國將軍、河東太守，代劉遵考守蒲阪。

translations.literal: Yu made Dezu supervise Hedong and Pingyang military affairs, general Who Supports the State, Administrator of Hedong, replacing Liu Zunkao to hold Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu gave him Hedong-Pingyang command, supporting-state general, Hedong magistrate, Puban garrison—replacing Liu Zunkao.

sentences.zh: 及河北覆敗，德祖全軍而歸。

translations.literal: When the Hebei front collapsed, Dezu brought the entire army back intact.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei's rout still saw Mao Dezu extract his corps whole.

sentences.zh: 裕方欲蕩平關洛，先以德祖督九郡軍事、冠軍將軍、滎陽京兆太守，以前後功，賜爵灌陽縣男，尋遷督司雍並三州諸軍事、冠軍將軍、司州刺史，戍武牢，為魏所沒。

translations.literal: Yu was about to level Guanzhong and Luoyang; first he made Dezu supervise nine commanderies' military affairs as Champion general and Administrator of Xingyang and Jingzhao; for successive merits he was granted Baron of Guanyang County; soon he was promoted supervisor of military affairs over Si, Yong, and Bing—three provinces—with Champion generalship and Inspectorship of Sizhou, garrisoning Wulao, where he was lost to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Before the next Guan-Luo push Liu Yu named Mao Dezu champion over nine counties, Xingyang-Jingzhao magistrate, Guanyang baron, then Si-Yong-Bing governor with Sizhou inspectorate at Wulao—where Wei took him.

sentences.zh: 德祖次弟嶷，嶷弟辯，並有志節。

translations.literal: Dezu's next younger brother Yi and Yi's younger brother Bian both possessed determination and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brothers Mao Yi and Mao Bian shared fierce integrity.

sentences.zh: 嶷死于盧循之難，辯沒于魯宗之役，並奮不顧命，為世所歎。

translations.literal: Yi died in Lu Xun's turmoil; Bian perished in Lu Zongzhi's campaign—both fought recklessly and were lamented by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Yi fell in Lu Xun's rising; Mao Bian in Lu Zongzhi's war—both charged without thought for life.

sentences.zh: 劉遐，字正長，廣平易陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xia, styled Zhengzhang, was a man of Yiyang in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xia, courtesy Zhengzhang, came from Yiyang in Guangping commandery.

sentences.zh: 性果毅，便弓馬，開豁勇壯。

translations.literal: By nature he was resolute, handy with bow and horse, open-hearted, brave, and strong.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and blunt, superb rider and archer, with fearless vigor.

sentences.zh: 值天下大亂，遐為塢主，每擊賊，率壯士陷堅摧鋒，冀方比之張飛、關羽。

translations.literal: When the realm fell into great chaos, Xia became fort master; whenever he struck bandits he led stalwarts to pierce armor and break spear-points; north of the Ji men compared him to Zhang Fei and Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Amid collapse he ruled a river fort, charging vanguard like Zhang Fei or Guan Yu whenever raiders neared.

sentences.zh: 鄉人冀州刺史邵續深器之，以女妻焉，遂壁於河濟之間，賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: His townsman Inspector of Jizhou Shao Xu deeply esteemed him and gave him a daughter in marriage; he therefore walled between the Yellow and Ji rivers and bandits dared not press him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu of Jizhou admired him, married him into the family, and backed his stockade between the rivers until foes feared the ground.

sentences.zh: 遐間道遣使受元帝節度，朝廷嘉之，璽書慰勉，以為龍驤將軍、平原內史。

translations.literal: Xia sent envoys by hidden paths to accept orders from Emperor Yuan; the court praised him with sealed edicts of comfort and encouragement and appointed him general Soaring Dragon and Interior Secretary of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Secret couriers pledged him to Emperor Yuan; the throne answered with praise and named him Soaring Dragon general and Pingyuan secretary.

sentences.zh: 建武初，元帝令曰：「遐忠勇果毅，義誠可嘉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwu era Emperor Yuan's order said: "Xia is loyal, brave, resolute, and righteous—conduct worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jianwu brought Yuan's writ: Liu Xia's loyalty and grit deserved honor.

sentences.zh: 以遐為下邳內史，將軍如故。」

translations.literal: " Appoint Xia Interior Secretary of Xiapi with generalship unchanged."
translations.idiomatic: " Make him Xiapi secretary while keeping his general's rank."

sentences.zh: 初，沛人周堅，一名撫，與同郡周默因天下亂，各為塢主，以寇抄為事。

translations.literal: At first Zhou Jian of Pei—also called Fu—and Zhou Mo of the same commandery, exploiting the realm's chaos, each became fort masters and lived by raiding.
translations.idiomatic: Pei natives Zhou Jian, alias Fu, and Zhou Mo crowned themselves fort chiefs and lived by plunder.

sentences.zh: 默降祖逖，撫怒，遂襲殺默，以彭城叛，石勒遣騎援之。

translations.literal: Mo surrendered to Zu Ti; Fu grew angry, attacked and killed Mo, rebelled at Pengcheng, and Shi Le sent cavalry to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mo yielded to Zu Ti; Zhou Fu slew him, seized Pengcheng, and won Shi Le's riders.

sentences.zh: 詔遐領彭城內史，與徐州刺史蔡豹、太山太守徐龕共討撫，戰於寒山，撫敗走。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xia to hold concurrent Interior Secretary of Pengcheng and together with Inspector of Xuzhou Cai Bao and Administrator of Taishan Xu Kan jointly punish Fu; they fought at Cold Mountain and Fu fled.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Liu Xia Pengcheng secretary alongside Cai Bao and Xu Kan; Cold Mountain broke Zhou Fu.

sentences.zh: 詔徙遐為臨淮太守。

translations.literal: An edict transferred Xia to Administrator of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Edict shifted him to Linhuai magistrate.

sentences.zh: 徐龕復反，事平，以遐為北中郎將、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: When Xu Kan rebelled again and the affair was settled, Xia was appointed general of the Northern Palace Court and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Kan's second revolt cleared, Liu Xia took northern palace rank and Yanzhou inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 子肇年幼，成帝以徐州授郗鑒，以郭默為北中郎將，領遐部曲。

translations.literal: His son Zhao was young; Emperor Cheng assigned Xuzhou to Xi Jian and Guo Mo as general of the Northern Palace Court to lead Xia's personal corps.
translations.idiomatic: Young Liu Zhao left Xuzhou to Xi Jian while Guo Mo absorbed Liu Xia's household troops.

sentences.zh: 遐妹夫田防及遐故將史迭、卞咸、李龍等不樂他屬，共立肇，襲遐故位以叛。

translations.literal: Xia's brother-in-law Tian Fang and Xia's old commanders Shi Die, Bian Xian, Li Long and others disliked serving another master; together they raised Zhao, seized Xia's former post, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Brother-in-law Tian Fang and veterans Shi Die, Bian Xian, and Li Long refused new masters, crowned boy Zhao, and mutinied.

sentences.zh: 成帝遣郭默等率諸郡討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng dispatched Guo Mo and others leading various commanderies to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo led county levies against them.

sentences.zh: 默等始上道，而臨淮太守劉矯率將士數百掩襲遐營，迭等迸走，斬田防及督護卞咸等，追斬迭、龍於下邳，傳首詣闕。

translations.literal: Hardly had Mo and company set out when Administrator of Linhuai Liu Jiao led several hundred officers and men in a surprise raid on Xia's camp; Die and others scattered in flight; Jiao beheaded Tian Fang and protector Bian Xian and others; pursuing, he cut down Die and Long at Xiapi and sent heads to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before Guo Mo marched, Liu Jiao of Linhuai stormed the fort, scattered the plotters, beheaded Tian Fang and Bian Xian, ran down Shi Die and Li Long at Xiapi, and shipped heads south.

sentences.zh: 遐母妻子參佐將士悉還建康。

translations.literal: Xia's mother, wife, children, staff, and soldiers all returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Mother, wives, children, aides, and troops reached Jiankang alive.

sentences.zh: 遐妻驍果有父風。

translations.literal: Xia's wife was fierce and resolute like her father.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xia's wife matched her father's ferocity.

sentences.zh: 遐嘗為石季龍所圍，妻單將數騎，拔遐出於萬眾之中。

translations.literal: Once when Xia was surrounded by Shi Jilong, his wife alone led several riders and pulled Xia free from amid tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Jilong ringed Liu Xia, she sliced through alone with a handful of horse and dragged him free.

sentences.zh: 及田防等欲為亂，遐妻止之，不從，乃密起火燒甲杖都盡。

translations.literal: When Tian Fang and others plotted revolt, Xia's wife stopped them; they would not listen, so she secretly set fires that burned armor and weapons to ash.
translations.idiomatic: She forbade Tian Fang's coup; ignored, she torched the armory.

sentences.zh: 肇襲爵，官至散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhao inherited the nobility and rose to Gentleman Cavalier Attendant at the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao inherited and climbed to palace gentleman attendant.

sentences.zh: 肇卒，子舉嗣。

translations.literal: When Zhao died, his son Ju inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ju followed Liu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 卒，子遵之嗣。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Dunzhi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Liu Dunzhi.

sentences.zh: 卒，子伯齡嗣。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Boling inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Boling succeeded.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Song received the abdication, the principality was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song erased the fief.

sentences.zh: 鄧岳，字伯山，陳郡人也。

translations.literal: Deng Yue, styled Boshan, was a man of Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yue, courtesy Boshan, came from Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 本名岳，以犯康帝諱，改為嶽，後竟改名為岱焉。

translations.literal: His original given name was Yue; because it violated Emperor Kang's taboo he changed it to Yue with the mountain radical, and later finally renamed himself Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Born Deng Yue, he swapped graphs for Kang's taboo to Deng Yue variant, then settled on Deng Dai.

sentences.zh: 少有將帥才略，為王敦參軍。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed strategic talent and became Wang Dun's aide.
translations.idiomatic: Young Deng Yue showed command gifts on Wang Dun's staff.

sentences.zh: 轉從事中郎、西陽太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred attendant clerk and Administrator of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion brought attendant clerk and Xiyang magistrate.

sentences.zh: 王含構產逆，嶽領兵隨含向京都。

translations.literal: When Wang Han plotted treason, Yue led troops following Han toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han's coup drew Deng Yue's column toward Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 及含敗，岳與周撫俱奔蠻王向蠶。

translations.literal: When Han was defeated, Yue fled together with Zhou Fu to the Yi chieftain Xiang Can.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat sent Deng Yue and Zhou Fu to Barbarian King Xiang Can.

sentences.zh: 後遇赦，與撫俱出。

translations.literal: Later encountering an amnesty, he emerged together with Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty freed him with Zhou Fu.

sentences.zh: 久之，司徒王導命為從事中郎，後復為西陽太守。

translations.literal: After a long while Minister of Education Wang Dao ordered him attendant clerk; later he again became Administrator of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao later restored him to attendant clerk and Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 及蘇峻反，平南將軍溫嶠遣嶽與督護王愆期、鄱陽太守紀睦等率舟軍赴難。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, general Who Pacifies the South Wen Qiao dispatched Yue together with protector Wang Yanqi, Administrator of Poyang Ji Mu, and others leading river forces to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun's rising saw Wen Qiao send Deng Yue, Wang Yanqi, and Ji Mu downstream.

sentences.zh: 峻平，還郡。

translations.literal: After Jun was crushed he returned to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Peace took him home to Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 郭默之殺劉胤也，大司馬陶侃使岳率西陽之眾討之。

translations.literal: When Guo Mo murdered Liu Yin, Grand Marshal Tao Kan ordered Yue to lead Xiyang's host against him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo's killing of Liu Yin brought Tao Kan's order for Deng Yue to march from Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 默平，遷督交廣二州軍事、建武將軍、領平越中郎將、廣州刺史、假節，錄前後勳，封宜城縣伯。

translations.literal: After Mo was crushed he was promoted to supervise military affairs of Jiao and Guang—two provinces—general Who Displays Martial Might, concurrent Colonel Who Pacifies the Yue, Inspector of Guangzhou with credential staff; recording successive merits he was enfeoffed Baron of Yicheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Victory stacked titles: Jiao-Guang overseer, mighty-display general, Yue colonel, Guangzhou inspector, credential staff, baron of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 咸康三年，嶽遣軍伐夜郎，破之，加督寧州，進征虜將軍，遷平南將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiankang Yue dispatched troops to attack Yelang, crushed them, added supervision of Ningzhou, advanced to general Who Conquers the Caitiffs, and was promoted general Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Xiankang third year brought conquest of Yelang, added Ningzhou watch, caitiff general, southern pacifier.

sentences.zh: 卒，子遐嗣。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Xia inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Deng Xia succeeded.

sentences.zh: 遐字應遠。

translations.literal: Xia styled Yingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Xia took courtesy Yingyuan.

sentences.zh: 勇力絕人，氣蓋當時，時人方之樊噲。

translations.literal: His courage and strength surpassed others and his spirit overshadowed the age; men of the time compared him to Fan Kuai.
translations.idiomatic: Strength and swagger rivaled Fan Kuai in gossip.

sentences.zh: 桓溫以為參軍，數從溫征伐，曆冠軍將軍，數郡太守，號為名將。

translations.literal: Huan Wen employed him as aide; he repeatedly followed Wen on campaigns, rose through Champion general and several magistracies, and was famed as a noted general.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's wars forged champion posts and county seats until Deng Xia ranked among storied captains.

sentences.zh: 襄陽城北沔水中有蛟，常為人害，遐遂拔劍入水，蛟繞其足，遐揮劍截蛟數段而出。

translations.literal: North of Xiangyang in the Han River lay a river-dragon that habitually harmed people; Xia drew his sword, entered the water, the dragon coiled his legs, and Xia slashed it into several segments and emerged.
translations.idiomatic: A river monster plagued Xiangyang; Deng Xia waded in, let it twist his legs, and carved it to pieces.

sentences.zh: 枋頭之役，溫既懷恥忿，且忌憚遐之勇果，因免遐官，尋卒。

translations.literal: At the Fangtou campaign Wen nursed shame and rage and also feared Xia's courage and resolution; therefore he dismissed Xia from office; soon Xia died.
translations.idiomatic: Fangtou's humiliation made Huan Wen jealous of Deng Xia's nerve—he stripped him and Xia died soon after.

sentences.zh: 甯康中，追贈廬陵太守。

translations.literal: During Ningkang he was posthumously honored Administrator of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Ningkang years posthumously named him Luling magistrate.

sentences.zh: 岳弟逸，字茂山，亦有武幹。

translations.literal: Yue's younger brother Yi, styled Maoshan, also possessed martial capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Deng Yi shared martial gifts.

sentences.zh: 嶽卒後，以逸監交廣州、建威將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史、假節。

translations.literal: After Yue died, Yi was appointed supervisor of Jiao and Guangzhou, general Who Displays Martial Might, Colonel Who Pacifies the Yue, Inspector of Guangzhou with credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yue's death handed Deng Yi Jiao-Guang command, mighty-display rank, Yue colonel, Guangzhou inspector, credential staff.

sentences.zh: 硃序，字次倫，義陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Xu, styled Cilun, was a man of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu, courtesy Cilun, hailed from Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 父燾，以才幹曆西蠻校尉、益州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Tao rose through talent to Colonel Who Subdues the Western Yi and Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Father Zhu Tao climbed to western Yi colonel and Yizhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 序世為名將，累遷鷹揚將軍、江夏相。

translations.literal: For generations the house produced noted generals; Xu was repeatedly promoted general Who Spreads Might and Chancellor of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Generals ran in the blood; Zhu Xu rose to spreading-might general and Jiangxia chancellor.

sentences.zh: 興甯末，梁州刺史司馬勳反，桓溫表序為征討都護往討之，以功拜征虜將軍，封襄平子。

translations.literal: Near the end of the Xingning era Inspector of Liangzhou Sima Xun rebelled; Huan Wen memorialized Xu as supreme protector for the punitive expedition; for merit he was appointed general Who Conquers the Caitiffs and enfeoffed Viscount of Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xun's Liangzhou revolt sent Zhu Xu under Huan Wen's banner—merit won caitiff general and Xiangping viscount.

sentences.zh: 太和中，遷兗州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Taihe era he was transferred Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe brought Yanzhou inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 時長城人錢弘聚党百餘人，藏匿原鄉山。

translations.literal: At that time Qian Hong of Changcheng gathered a band of over a hundred men and hid on Yuanxiang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Hong holed up on Yuanxiang Mountain with a hundred blades.

sentences.zh: 以序為中軍司馬、吳興太守。

translations.literal: Xu was appointed marshal of the Central Army and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Court named Zhu Xu central army marshal and Wuxing magistrate.

sentences.zh: 序至郡，討擒之。

translations.literal: When Xu reached the commandery he attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He swept the hills and caged Qian Hong.

sentences.zh: 事訖，還兗州。

translations.literal: When the affair concluded he returned to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Duty done, he reclaimed Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 甯康初，拜使持節、監沔中諸軍事、南中郎將、梁州刺史，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ningkang he was appointed credential bearer, supervisor of all military affairs on the Han River, General of the Southern Palace Court, Inspector of Liangzhou, garrisoning Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ningkang opened with credential staff, Han River command, southern palace general, Liangzhou inspector at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 是歲，苻堅遣其將苻不等率眾圍序，序固守，賊糧將盡，率眾苦攻之。

translations.literal: That year Fu Jian dispatched general Fu Bu and others leading a host to besiege Xu; Xu held firm; enemy grain nearly exhausted and they pressed the assault with full strength.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's Fu Bu besieged Xiangyang until supplies failed, then hurled desperate assaults.

sentences.zh: 初，苻丕之來攻也，序母韓自登城履行，謖西北角當先受弊，遂領百餘婢並城中女子於其角斜築城二十餘丈。

translations.literal: At first, when Fu Bu came to attack, Xu's mother Lady Han herself climbed the wall to inspect and judged the northwest corner would suffer harm first; she therefore led more than a hundred maids together with women of the city to build slanting ramparts twenty-plus zhang at that corner.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Han walked the walls, saw the northwest would buckle first, and piled twenty-plus zhang of earth there with maids and townswomen.

sentences.zh: 賊攻西北角，果潰，眾便固新築城。

translations.literal: The bandits assaulted the northwest corner and it indeed collapsed; the host then held firm on the newly built wall.
translations.idiomatic: The foe smashed the old northwest shoulder; defenders slid onto Lady Han's fresh berm.

sentences.zh: 丕遂引退。

translations.literal: Bu therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bu quit the siege.

sentences.zh: 襄陽人謂此城為夫人城。

translations.literal: People of Xiangyang call this rampart Lady's Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Locals still call it the Lady's Wall.

sentences.zh: 序累戰破賊，人情勞懈，又以賊退稍遠，疑未能來，守備不謹，督護李伯護密與賊相應，襄陽遂沒，序陷於苻堅。

translations.literal: Xu repeatedly fought and defeated bandits; morale grew weary and lax; moreover because the bandits had withdrawn somewhat far he doubted they would come again and guarding grew careless; protector Li Bohu secretly communicated with bandits; Xiangyang therefore fell and Xu was trapped by Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Victory bred slack; Zhu Xu assumed distance meant peace; Li Bohu betrayed the gates to Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 堅殺伯護徇之，以其不忠也。

translations.literal: Jian executed Bohu as a warning because he was disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian executed Li Bohu as the traitor he was.

sentences.zh: 序欲逃歸，潛至宜陽，藏夏揆家。

translations.literal: Xu wished to flee home and secretly reached Yiyang, hiding with Xia Kui's household.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu slipped toward Jin lines and hid with Xia Kui.

sentences.zh: 堅疑揆，收之，序乃詣苻暉自首，堅嘉而不問，以為尚書。

translations.literal: Jian suspected Kui and seized him; Xu therefore presented himself to Fu Hui to confess; Jian praised him and did not punish him, appointing him minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion fell on Xia Kui; Zhu Xu surrendered to Fu Hui instead and Fu Jian admired him into minister rank.

sentences.zh: 太元中，苻堅南侵，謝石率眾距之。

translations.literal: During the Taiyuan era Fu Jian invaded south and Xie Shi led troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan brought Fu Jian south against Xie Shi.

sentences.zh: 時堅大兵尚在項，苻融以三十萬眾先至。

translations.literal: At that time Jian's main army was still at Xiang; Fu Rong arrived first with three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's core host lingered at Xiang while Fu Rong landed three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 堅遣序說謝石，稱己兵威。

translations.literal: Jian dispatched Xu to persuade Xie Shi, boasting his army's might.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent Zhu Xu to awe Xie Shi with numbers.

sentences.zh: 序反謂石曰：「若堅百萬之眾悉到，莫可與敵，及其未會，擊之，可以得志。

translations.literal: Xu instead told Shi: "If Jian's million troops all arrive none can oppose them; strike before they assemble and you may succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu whispered: wait for the million and you lose—hit Fu Jian now while columns straggle.

sentences.zh: 」於是石遣謝琰選勇士八千人涉肥水挑戰。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Shi dispatched Xie Yan to pick eight thousand warriors to ford the Fei River and offer challenge.
translations.idiomatic: " Xie Shi ordered Xie Yan across the Fei with eight thousand picked men.

sentences.zh: 堅眾小卻，序時在其軍後，唱云：「堅敗！

translations.literal: Jian's host stepped slightly back; Xu was then behind their lines and shouted: "Jian is defeated!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's lines eased backward; Zhu Xu howled from the rear that Fu Jian had fallen.

sentences.zh: 」眾遂大奔，序乃得歸。

translations.literal: " The host thereupon fled in panic and Xu was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: " Panic routed Fu Jian and Zhu Xu sprinted home.

sentences.zh: 拜龍驤將軍、琅邪內史，轉揚州豫州五郡軍事、豫州刺史，屯洛陽。
