translations.literal: He was appointed general Soaring Dragon, Interior Secretary of Langye, transferred supervisor of military affairs over five Yangzhou and Yuzhou commanderies with Inspectorship of Yuzhou, garrisoning Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards piled: Soaring Dragon, Langye secretary, five-county Yang-Yu command, Yuzhou inspector at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後丁零翟遼反，序遣將軍秦膺、童斌與淮泗諸郡共討之。

translations.literal: Later Dingling chief Zhai Liao rebelled; Xu dispatched generals Qin Ying and Tong Bin together with Huai and Si commanderies to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Liao's Dingling revolt drew Qin Ying and Tong Bin from Zhu Xu.

sentences.zh: 又監兗青二州諸軍事、二州刺史，將軍如故，進鎮彭城。

translations.literal: He additionally supervised military affairs of Yan and Qing—two provinces—with concurrent dual inspectorship, general as before, advancing headquarters to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He added Yan-Qing oversight, twin inspectors, old rank, Pengcheng seat.

sentences.zh: 序求鎮淮陰，帝許焉。

translations.literal: Xu requested to garrison Huaiyin; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He traded up for Huaiyin and the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 翟遼又使其子釗寇陳潁，序還遣秦膺討釗，走之，拜征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Zhai Liao again sent his son Zhai Zhao to raid Chen and Ying; Xu returned and dispatched Qin Ying against Zhao, drove him off, and was appointed general Who Conquers the Caitiffs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Liao's son Zhai Zhao raided Chen-Ying; Qin Ying threw him back and Zhu Xu gained caitiff general.

sentences.zh: 表求運江州米十萬斛，布五千匹以資軍費，詔聽之。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting one hundred thousand hu of grain from Jiangzhou and five thousand bolts of cloth to supply military expenses; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: He begged one hundred thousand hu from Jiangzhou plus five thousand bolts—approved.

sentences.zh: 加都督司、雍、梁、秦四州軍事。

translations.literal: He was additionally named supervisor of military affairs over Si, Yong, Liang, and Qin—four provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Four-province Si-Yong-Liang-Qin command followed.

sentences.zh: 帝遣廣威將軍、河南太守楊佺期，南陽太守趙睦，各領兵千人隸序。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched general Who Displays Martial Glory and Administrator of Henan Yang Quanqi and Administrator of Nanyang Zhao Mu, each leading a thousand men under Xu's command.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Quanqi of Henan and Zhao Mu of Nanyang brought a thousand men each to Zhu Xu.

sentences.zh: 序又表求故荊州刺史桓石生府田百頃，並谷八萬斛，給之。

translations.literal: Xu further memorialized requesting the hundred qing of farmland and eighty thousand hu of grain formerly attached to former Inspector of Jingzhou Huan Shisheng's office; they were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed Huan Shisheng's hundred qing and eighty thousand hu—granted.

sentences.zh: 仍戍洛陽，衛山陵也。

translations.literal: He still garrisoned Luoyang to guard the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed at Luoyang guarding Jin mausolea.

sentences.zh: 其後慕容永率眾向洛陽，序自河陰北濟，與永偽將王次等相遇，乃戰于沁水，次改走，斬其支將勿支首。

translations.literal: Later Murong Yong led troops toward Luoyang; Xu crossed north from Heyin, encountered Yong's deputy Wang Ci and others, fought at the Qin River—Ci fled—and beheaded deputy Wuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong drew Zhu Xu north from Heyin; Qin River broke Wang Ci and took Wuzhi's head.

sentences.zh: 參軍趙睦、江夏相桓不才追永，破之於太行。

translations.literal: Aides Zhao Mu and Chancellor of Jiangxia Huan Bucai pursued Yong and defeated him at Taihang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Mu and Huan Bucai chased Murong Yong into Taihang and broke him.

sentences.zh: 永歸上黨。

translations.literal: Yong returned to Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong fled to Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 時楊楷聚眾數千，在湖陝，聞永敗，遣任子詣序乞降。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Kai gathered several thousand men at Huxia; hearing Yong's defeat he sent heir Ren to Xu seeking surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kai at Huxia offered surrender after Yong's rout.

sentences.zh: 序追永至上黨之白水，與永相持二旬。

translations.literal: Xu pursued Yong to Baishui in Shangdang and faced him for twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu dogged Murong Yong to Baishui for twenty days.

sentences.zh: 聞翟遼欲向金墉，乃還，遂攻翟釗于石門，遣參軍趙蕃破翟遼於懷縣，遼宵遁。

translations.literal: Hearing Zhai Liao meant to strike the Golden Rampart fortress he returned, attacked Zhai Zhao at Stone Gate, dispatched aide Zhao Fan to defeat Zhai Liao at Huai County; Liao fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: News of Zhai Liao aiming at Golden Rampart spun Zhu Xu back—Stone Gate struck Zhai Zhao, Zhao Fan whipped Zhai Liao at Huai, who vanished overnight.

sentences.zh: 序退次洛陽，留鷹揚將軍硃党戍石門。

translations.literal: Xu withdrew to halt at Luoyang and left general Who Spreads Might Zhu Dang to hold Stone Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He regrouped at Luoyang leaving Zhu Dang at Stone Gate.

sentences.zh: 序仍使子略督護洛城，趙蕃為助。

translations.literal: Xu still ordered son Lue to supervise defense of Luoyang city with Zhao Fan assisting.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhu Lue guarded Luoyang with Zhao Fan.

sentences.zh: 序還襄陽。

translations.literal: Xu returned to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu rode home to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 會稽王道子以序勝負相補，不加褒貶。

translations.literal: Prince of Kuaiji Wang Daozi deemed Xu's victories and defeats balanced each other and added neither praise nor blame.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daozi judged Zhu Xu's wins and losses a wash—no medal, no lash.

sentences.zh: 其後東羌校尉竇沖欲入漢川，安定人皇甫釗、京兆人周勳等謀納之。

translations.literal: Later Colonel of the Eastern Qiang Dou Chong wished to enter Hanzhong; Huangfu Zhao of Anding and Zhou Xun of Jingzhao plotted to admit him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong aimed at Hanzhong; Huangfu Zhao and Zhou Xun meant to open the gate.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史周瓊失巴西三郡，眾寡力弱，告急於序，序遣將軍皇甫貞率眾赴之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Liangzhou Zhou Qiong lost three Ba-Xi commanderies; his host was few and weak; he urgently appealed to Xu; Xu dispatched general Huangfu Zhen with troops to hurry there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qiong's triple loss brought Zhu Xu's column under Huangfu Zhen.

sentences.zh: 沖據長安東，釗、勳散走。

translations.literal: Chong occupied east of Chang'an; Zhao and Xun scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong seized Chang'an's east flank while plotters ran.

sentences.zh: 序以老病，累表解職，不許。

translations.literal: Xu, citing age and illness, repeatedly memorialized to resign; permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Age and sickness drove resignation pleas—denied.

sentences.zh: 詔斷表，遂輒去任。

translations.literal: An edict cut off memorials; he nevertheless departed post.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts barred more excuses; he quit anyway.

sentences.zh: 數旬，歸罪廷尉，詔原不問。

translations.literal: After several tens of days he surrendered himself to the minister of justice; an edict pardoned him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He presented himself to the minister of justice and won blanket pardon.

sentences.zh: 太元十八年卒，贈左將軍、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He died in the eighteenth year of Taiyuan; posthumously honored general of the Left with ordinary attendant cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan eighteen ended his life; posthumous left general and ordinary attendant followed.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：晉氏淪喪，播遷江表，內難薦臻，外虞不息，經略之道，是所未弘，將帥之功，無聞焉爾。

translations.literal: The historians remark: When Jin lost the Central Plains and shifted south of the Yangzi, inner calamities piled up without cease and outer peril never rested—the arts of grand strategy were never broadly developed, and true merit among generals is scarcely heard.
translations.idiomatic: Historians add: refugee Jin faced coup within and raid without—little grand strategy, thinner laurels for captains.

sentences.zh: 遜、豹、宣、胤服勤於太興之間，毛、鄧、劉、硃馳騖乎咸和之後。

translations.literal: Xun, Bao, Xuan, and Yin bore heavy service between the Taixing years; Mao, Deng, Liu, and Zhu raced their chargers after the Xianhe era.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun, Cai Bao, Huan Xuan, and Liu Yin wore themselves out in Emperor Yuan's Taixing reign; Mao Bao, Deng Yue, Liu Xia, and Zhu Si chased glory once Xianhe arrived.

sentences.zh: 雖人不逮古，亦足列於當世焉。

translations.literal: Although none matched men of high antiquity, they still suffice to stand among peers of their own age.
translations.idiomatic: They fell short of legendary exemplars yet deserved places among their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：氣分淮海，災流瀍澗。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Vital breath split Huai and sea; disaster spilled Chan and Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Verdict runs: fortune fractured between Huai and the eastern sea; calamity flooded the Chan and Jian valleys.

sentences.zh: 覆類玄蚖，興微《鴻雁》。

translations.literal: Ruin wrapped folk like black creeping things; amid faint revival sounded 《Wild Geese》.
translations.idiomatic: Collapse coiled like shadow reptiles; even faint renewal echoed 《Wild Geese》 on weary wings.

sentences.zh: 鼓鞞在聽，《兔罝》有作。

translations.literal: War-drums filled every ear; 《The Rabbit Snare》 found makers once more.
translations.idiomatic: Battle drums hammered the courts; recruiting songs such as 《The Rabbit Snare》 rang out again.

sentences.zh: 赳赳群英，勤茲王略。

translations.literal: Bold, bold that band of champions—they strained every nerve for the royal plan.
translations.idiomatic: Staunch captains shouldered the throne's wider strategy with relentless grit.
